Allah mentioned 'Ad and Thamud because the Arabs knew them: they passed by the dwellings of Thamud when travelling to al-Sham, and they knew the location of 'Ad, al-Ahqaf, and they related and transmitted what befell them of punishment. Otherwise, there were also other peoples whom Allah the Mighty and Majestic destroyed, but since these people, meaning 'Ad and Thamud, were the ones the Arabs (i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah) knew, He specified them: ﴿like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud﴾. ﴿'Ad﴾ were the people of Hud, and ﴿Thamud﴾ were the people of Salih.

'Ad were destroyed by the wind, and the wisdom behind this was that Allah the Mighty and Majestic would show them their weakness, for they had boasted of their strength and said: ﴿Who is stronger than us in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 15]. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is stronger than them in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 15]. As for Thamud, Allah the Mighty and Majestic destroyed them with a rajfah and a cry: they were cried upon, and the earth was shaken beneath them, and they perished.

﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them﴾ [Fussilat 14], to the end of the verse. ﴿When (idh)﴾ here is an adverb of causation, meaning it explains the cause of the thunderbolt that destroyed them: the reason was that the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them. The mufassir said: (i.e., coming to them and turning away from them, and they disbelieved as will be explained, and the destruction was only in their time).

﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them﴾. As for His saying ﴿from before them and from behind them﴾: the author said: (i.e., coming to them and turning away from them). That is, at times they came and called to them, and at times they turned away and threatened them if they did not believe. It is possible that what is meant by ﴿from before them and from behind them﴾ is that they came to them with the past verses and the future verses, so they did not fall short in making the truth clear, but brought the clarification of the truth from every direction.

His saying: (they disbelieved). This is the purpose of the warning: that they disbelieved and were therefore destroyed. For this reason he said: (and the destruction was only in their time), i.e., in the time of disbelief, and not in the time of the coming (of the messengers), because the messengers came first, then called and called again. When they persisted in their disbelief, they were destroyed. (That ﴿أن﴾ meaning ﴿not you worship except Allah﴾.) The author, may Allah have mercy on him, informed us that (أن) here is a verbal (maṣdariyyah) particle, and the implied meaning is: ﴿that you not worship﴾. That is, the messengers came with the command not to worship other than Allah. It is also possible that (أن) is explanatory (tafsiriyyah), because what precedes it contains the meaning of speech without its letters, since the messengers came with words and revelation which they spoke; so there is in it the meaning of speech without its letters. Whenever (أن) comes after something that contains the meaning of speech without its letters, they call it explanatory, such as His saying: ﴿So We revealed to him: Build the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation﴾ [al-Mu'minun 27], i.e., We revealed: build the ship.

﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee: Take for yourself (ann ittakhidhi)﴾ [al-Nahl 68]: here ﴿أن﴾ is explanatory. So whenever ﴿أن﴾ comes after something that contains the meaning of speech without its letters, it is explanatory. Accordingly, ﴿أن﴾ here may be maṣdariyyah, as the mufassir followed, or tafsiriyyah.

This disagreement determines how we parse (لا). If we parse ﴿أن﴾ as maṣdariyyah, then (لا) is a negation particle, and the verb is in the subjunctive mood governed by ﴿أن﴾. If we parse it as tafsiriyyah, then (لا) is a prohibitive particle, and the verb is in the jussive mood governed by (لا).

So the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of ﴿تعبدوا (ta'budu)﴾ depends on the disagreement over what? Over ﴿أن﴾. Say it, brother! If we make it tafsiriyyah, the verb is jussive governed by what?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: How do you parse the verb if ﴿أن﴾ is tafsiriyyah?
* Student: A present-tense verb in the jussive mood governed by the prohibitive (لا).
* The Shaykh: Well done, a present-tense verb in the jussive mood governed by the prohibitive (لا). And if we parse (أن) as maṣdariyyah?
* Student: In the subjunctive mood, governed by ﴿أن﴾.
* The Shaykh: In the subjunctive mood governed by ﴿أن﴾, exactly. On this view, (لا) is a negation particle, attached with the fa', and on the first view it is prohibitive.

﴿That you not worship except Allah, they said﴾ [Fussilat 14], to the end. (Not worship except Allah) is the meaning of the statement (There is no god but Allah), because (no god) means there is no truly worshipped one except Allah. Here it says (not worship except Allah), so it has the meaning of (There is no god but Allah). It has the same meaning as His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him: There is no god but I, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya' 25].

Whenever a person realises this statement (There is no god but Allah), he must perform obedience to Allah, necessarily. As long as you testify that there is no god but Allah, you must take the means that bring you to this God whom you have testified to be the only god.

﴿They said﴾: who is the subject? The people of 'Ad and Thamud. (﴿They said: If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down﴾ angels upon us, ﴿and indeed we, in what you have been sent with, are disbelievers﴾ on your claim.)

This answer is an extremely feeble one: if our Lord had willed that we be guided and not worship other than Allah, He would have sent down angels. On this reckoning which I told you about, the object of ﴿willed﴾ is omitted, i.e., if our Lord had willed that we not worship except Him, He would have sent down angels. So ﴿law (if)﴾ is conditional, ﴿shā'a (willed)﴾ is the verb of the condition, and the answer of the condition is ﴿la-anzala malā'ikah (He would have sent down angels)﴾ [Fussilat 14], and the object of ﴿shā'a﴾ is omitted; the implied meaning is: if He had willed that we not worship except Him, He would have sent down angels.

This argument is a false argument, because those sent to them, were they angels or humans? Answer me!
* The students: Humans.
* The Shaykh: Humans, there is no problem there. So how would Allah send angels to humans? Moreover, Allah said in answer to this: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel, We would have made him a man﴾; that is, in the form of a man. It is impossible for Him to send down an angel in the form of an angel to humans. Even if it were supposed that Allah sent down an angel, He would make him in the form of a human. And then the doubt returns: ﴿and We would have confused them about what they are confusing﴾ [al-An'am 9]. Do you see that if Allah sent to the children of Adam Gabriel with six hundred wings, filling the horizon, would people be able to stand in harmony with him? Never! Rather they would flee from him and would not stand before him. If that is so, this argument collapses, because we say to these people and to whoever says what they say: if Allah had sent down an angel, He would have made him a man, and then the doubt returns.

So the argument is false: ﴿He would have sent down angels﴾. As for His saying: ﴿If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down﴾ upon us ﴿angels, then indeed we, in what you have been sent with, are disbelievers﴾: the fa' here is for inference (tafri'), i.e., based on the supposition that He did not send down angels, we are disbelievers in what you were sent with.

We seek Allah's protection from such disbelief. They affirmed their disbelief and said: ﴿in what you have been sent with, we are disbelievers﴾. The object was placed first, because ﴿in what you have been sent with﴾ is related to ﴿disbelievers﴾, so why was it placed before it? For two reasons. The first reason: to observe the rhyme of the verses (fawasil). If he had said: ﴿then indeed we are disbelievers in what you have been sent with﴾, the rhymes would not have matched. When he said: ﴿in what you have been sent with, are disbelievers﴾, the rhymes matched, and observing harmony is an established principle. Consider Musa and Harun: which of them is better?
* The students: Musa.
* The Shaykh: And who is mentioned first in the Quran?
* Students: Harun.
* The Shaykh: Musa, people, where are you?! Except in one verse, for the sake of harmony. In surah Ta-Ha Allah mentioned that the sorcerers said: ﴿They said: We believe in the Lord of Harun and Musa﴾ [Ta-Ha 70], although they had said: ﴿We believe in the Lord﴾ [al-A'raf 121] ﴿of Musa and Harun﴾ [al-A'raf 122]. This was the statement of the sorcerers, but when Allah related it in surah Ta-Ha He placed Harun first, for the harmony of the verses, even though Musa is better. And it was Musa whom the sorcerers mentioned first, as in several verses. But Allah the Mighty and Majestic related their words in surah Ta-Ha with Harun first. Why?
* The students: For the harmony of the rhymes.
* The Shaykh: Yes, for the harmony of the rhymes. Here, ﴿in what you have been sent with, are disbelievers﴾: the complement, which is ﴿in what you have been sent with﴾, was placed before the item it governs, for two reasons. The first reason: observing the rhymes. The second reason: restriction (hasr). As if these deniers, obstinate ones, said: If we believed in everything, we would still disbelieve in what you have been sent with. So it is as if they are saying: we disbelieve in nothing except what you have been sent with. Placing what should be later earlier conveys restriction.

Look at the obstinacy: ﴿in what you have been sent with, are disbelievers﴾. It is as if they said: we disbelieve only in what you have been sent with. This is the meaning of restriction, so it is more emphatic in obstinacy, as if they are saying: even if we believed in everything, we would never believe in what you have been sent with.

Moreover, His saying ﴿in what you have been sent with﴾ was said in the manner of feigned concession (tanazzul). For this reason the mufassir said: (on your claim). We say they said it by way of feigned concession, because if they had said it as an acknowledgement, they would have believed and become believers. But they said it by way of feigned concession: ﴿in what you have been sent with, are disbelievers﴾.

In this verse, the Prophet (ﷺ) is commanded to warn these deniers of a punishment like that of those before them, from His saying: ﴿Then say: I have warned you﴾ [Fussilat 13].

* Among the benefits of this verse: the establishment of qiyas (analogical reasoning). Warning the deniers would have no purpose if the meaning were not to compare the situation of those who denied the Messenger with the situation of those who denied Hud and Salih. Were it not for qiyas, this warning would have no benefit. So it permits qiyas and reasoning by way of an analogous and similar case. Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿There was in their stories a lesson for people of understanding﴾ [Yusuf 111]. The establishment of qiyas as evidence is one of the excellences of the Sharia, because establishing qiyas as evidence is what sound reason requires, since reason can never distinguish between two alike things.

Accordingly, those who denied qiyas have contradicted both the textual evidence and the rational evidence: those who denied it and said there is no qiyas in the Sharia. Glory be to Allah! The whole Quran points to this; all the parables in the Quran are proof of qiyas, without doubt, otherwise there would be no benefit in the parable. The Sunnah also came with qiyas: ﴿Tell me, if your mother had a debt, would you pay it? Pay Allah's debt, for Allah has more right to be paid.﴾ [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1852) and Muslim (1148/155), from Ibn 'Abbas]. They too contradict reason, because if qiyas were not established, the Sharia would be deficient, since it would not unite two alike cases. So in this verse there is the establishment of qiyas.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the messengers came to their peoples from every direction, coming and turning away, showing them the past verses and the future verses, but there was no benefit.

* Among the benefits of these noble verses: the messengers, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon them, came with the realisation of tawhid (monotheism), from His saying: ﴿that you not worship except Allah﴾ [Fussilat 14]. This is the fundamental principle to which all the messengers called. What is the evidence that they were all messengers who called to this?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, saying: Worship Allah and avoid the taghut﴾ [al-Nahl 36]. Is there a verse more explicit than this?
* Student: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him: There is no god but I, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya' 25].
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is explicit: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him: There is no god but I, so worship Me﴾. We mentioned in His saying: ﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them, that you not worship except Allah﴾ [Fussilat 14] that the author says: (coming to them and turning away from them). We mentioned another meaning: We brought them the past and future verses. And there also occurred to my mind just now: ﴿from before them﴾ means the messengers who came to them directly, i.e., Thamud were come to by Salih, and 'Ad were come to by Hud.
﴿From behind them﴾ means the earlier messengers. For this reason He said: ﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them﴾. It is known that the one sent to 'Ad was Hud, and to Thamud was Salih, and they are two, while ﴿messengers﴾ is plural. This implies that the meaning is: when the earlier and later messengers came to them. This is probably the most likely of the three possibilities.

* Among the benefits of these noble verses: the people of falsehood make comparisons with what has no real basis. They rejected the call of the messengers with what could not be a valid rejection. What is it with which they rejected it?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, not what they rejected it with. What is their doubt?
* Student: ﴿They said: If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels﴾ [Fussilat 14].
* The Shaykh: Well done. Is this doubt a proof?
* Student: No, it is not a proof.
* The Shaykh: It is not a proof. What is your evidence that it is not a proof?
* Student: The evidence is that Allah the Mighty and Majestic says in another verse: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them about what they are confusing﴾ [al-An'am 9]. So if Allah the Mighty and Majestic had sent down angels, He would have made them men, and the doubt would return.
* The Shaykh: Correct.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the intensity of the obstinacy of the deniers of Salih and 'Ad.
* Student: Hud.
* The Shaykh: Yes, Hud, well done. What is its aspect?
* Student: That even with the establishment of the messengership for them, they insist on their obstinacy and (...).
* The Shaykh: Also, is there another aspect we pointed out?
* Student: That by their saying this they restricted their denial...
* The Shaykh: Their disbelief.
* Student: They restricted their disbelief to what their messengers brought.
* The Shaykh: As if they are saying: if we believed in everything, we would not believe in what you have been sent with specifically. The specificity is conveyed by placing the prepositional phrase before the item it governs.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the deniers of the messengers believe in the angels while being disbelievers, from His saying: ﴿they would have sent down angels﴾.

* Also among its benefits: whoever affirms Lordship (rububiyyah) alone is not considered a believer until he affirms divinity (uluhiyyah), from His saying: ﴿If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels﴾. Likewise, the disbelievers among whom the Messenger (ﷺ) was sent were affirmers of Lordship: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say: The Mighty, the All-Knowing created them﴾ [al-Zukhruf 9]; ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say: Allah﴾ [al-Zukhruf 87]. But belief in Lordship is not sufficient for a person to be a Muslim; belief in divinity is necessary in addition to belief in Lordship. Which of them necessitates the other, and which includes the other? What necessitates the other: whoever believes in Lordship is necessarily obliged to believe in divinity. So the necessitating one is Lordship, and whoever believes in divinity has included in his belief the belief in Lordship. Is this clear?
* The students: Clear.
* The Shaykh: So one of them includes the other, and the second necessitates the other.

Also, among the signs of their obstinacy: they emphasized their disbelief with *inna* (إن), saying: ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent.﴾ Their emphasis on their disbelief and obstinacy is therefore expressed in several ways. First, the emphasis with *inna* (إن, "indeed"). Second, restriction (al-hasr), which is achieved by placing before its verb what should properly come after it, namely by placing the prepositional phrase before the element it modifies. Third, they used a nominal sentence (al-jumla al-ismiyya), which indicates permanence and continuity, unlike a verbal sentence, which indicates occurrence and non-continuity. Here they used the nominal sentence, which indicates permanence and continuity.

* Student: His saying, ﴿whom the Mighty, the All-Knowing created﴾, indicates that the disbelievers used to affirm God's unity in His names and attributes?

* Shaykh: They may have, and they may have affirmed some of the names and attributes, because they denied the Most Merciful (al-Rahman).

* Student: Some?

* Shaykh: Yes, some. Without doubt, they affirmed some of them.

* Student: (...) facing forward or turning away (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, there are three possibilities. The first is what the author said. The second is facing towards the signs and turning away from them, meaning the preceding signs and the following signs. The third is the earlier and later messengers.

* Student: His saying, ﴿and it was smoke﴾ [Fussilat 11], was the smoke before the creation of the heavens and the earth ancient?

* Shaykh: No. Previously it was water, then vapor formed from this water when God created the earth.

* Student: "(ʿĀd and Thamūd)": I mean regarding the grammatical aspect, i.e., the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of: ﴿Say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd﴾ [Fussilat 13]. ﴿Thamūd⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿ is coordinated with what?

* Shaykh: With ﴿ʿĀd﴾.

* Student: And ﴿ʿĀd﴾ is in the genitive?

* Shaykh: And ﴿Thamūd﴾ is in the genitive?

* Student: No, it is not in the genitive; it is in the accusative.

* Shaykh: What is not in the genitive? It is in the genitive. It is certain that it is in the genitive.

* Student: No, we have something that is not in the genitive.

* Shaykh: Show us with someone else!! ﴿And to Thamūd, their brother Ṣāliḥ﴾ [al-Aʿraf 73]. In ﴿to Thamūd﴾, ﴿to﴾ is not a preposition?!

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: And ﴿Thamūd⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿?

* Student: Accusative.

* Shaykh: Genitive. Apparently you have not studied grammar? Yes, say yes or no?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: You have not studied?

* Student: I have studied a little.

* Shaykh: Yes. Then be patient until you learn and it becomes clear to you. Tell me: is ﴿Thamūd⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿ accusative or genitive? You.

* Student: Genitive.

* Shaykh: How is it genitive when it has a fatḥa (فتحة)?

* Student: It is genitive, and its sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, because it is ghayr munṣarif (diptote, not declinable with nunation).

* Shaykh: Yes. Look, brother: the diptote is put in the genitive with a fatḥa and takes no tanwin.

* Student: Yes, what is its cause, I mean the reason?

* Shaykh: The reason is the Arabic language.

* Student: Shaykh, regarding His saying, ﴿the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Fussilat 12], how can we deduce the third attribute from the pairing of these two names?

* Shaykh: Might and knowledge. The combination of might and knowledge is perfection, because the Mighty without knowledge may strike out of ignorance, and the All-Knowing without might is weak.

* Student: The statement that He, glorified and exalted, mentioned about the people of ʿĀd and Thamūd, their saying: ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿ (...). Is it the wording that the people actually said, or is it according to the condition and speech of their state?

* Shaykh: No, they said it.

* Student: They said this exact wording?

* Shaykh: No. Their language was not Arabic, but God relates it from them in meaning.

* Student: And the Arabs?

* Shaykh: The Arabs? What about the Arabs?

* Student: (...) the disbelievers of Quraysh (...).

* Shaykh: No, this is a report about ʿĀd and Thamūd. But Quraysh denied the Messenger, as is well known.

* Student: Relating this doubt from them (...), relating it is sufficient to refute it, or to answer it in another verse.

* Shaykh: It is said: merely conceiving this statement is sufficient to refute and nullify it. Indeed, even the disbelievers of Quraysh said such things in Surat al-Anʿam: ﴿They say: "Why has no angel been sent down to him?" Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and they would not be reprieved. And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them as they confuse themselves. And messengers before you were certainly mocked﴾ [al-Anʿam 8–10].

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿So as for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right, and said, "Who is mightier than us in strength?" Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they were denying Our signs.﴾ (15) ﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind in days of ill omen, that We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.﴾ [Fussilat 15–16].

* **Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, said, when He mentioned the command to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to warn the Quraysh with a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud, that He would explain what happened to 'Ad and what happened to Thamud. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So as for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right.﴾ The word (ammā, "as for") is a conditional and distinguishing particle. As for its being a conditional particle, it is because it has a condition and a response: ﴿So as for 'Ad, they were arrogant﴾. As for its being a distinguishing particle, it is because it comes in that sense too: ﴿As for him who gives and fears (Allah) (5), and believes in the best reward﴾ [al-Layl 5–6], and ﴿As for him who is miserly and considers himself self-sufficient (8), and denies the best reward﴾ [al-Layl 8–9]. So it is a particle of condition and distinction.

﴿So as for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right.﴾ "Istakbarū" means: pride overtook them. The sīn and tā' were added for emphasis, meaning they became exceedingly proud.

His saying ﴿without right﴾ is not a restrictive qualifier but a clarifying qualifier, because every arrogance in the land is without right. Arrogance does not divide into two kinds; it is one kind, so every arrogance is without right. Such a qualifier is called a clarifying qualifier (ṣifah kāshifah), meaning it reveals what came before and shows its reality. So what is the reality of arrogance? That it is without right. Right is the opposite of falsehood, and falsehood is either in a statement or in a demand. Falsehood in a statement is lying, and falsehood in judgment is injustice. The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿and that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood﴾ [al-Hajj 62] includes both matters: it includes their claim that these are gods, which is a false claim, and it includes their act of worshipping these gods, which is injustice and wrongdoing, since they equate the created with the Creator.

﴿And they said﴾, meaning as part of what they were arrogant about. (﴿They said﴾ when they were warned of punishment: ﴿"Who is mightier than us in strength?"﴾) meaning: no one. The interrogative ﴿man﴾ here carries the sense of negation and denial. We have repeatedly mentioned that when the interrogative has the meaning of denial and negation, it becomes more emphatic than plain negation, because it contains a challenge.

﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ As you know, ﴿man﴾ is an interrogative noun, ﴿ashaddu﴾ is the predicate of the subject, because ﴿man﴾ is the subject and ﴿ashaddu﴾ is its predicate, and ﴿quwwatan﴾ is a specifying accusative (tamyīz) for ﴿ashaddu﴾. Among the general rules is that when a noun in the accusative comes after a comparative form, it is a tamyīz. ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ means no one.

Then the author mentioned an example of their strength. He said: (Each one of them would uproot a huge rock from the mountain and place it wherever he wished.) This example may be true, or it may be from the Isra'iliyyat (narrations from Israelite sources), because it is known that 'Ad were what?

* **Student:** They carved.

* **Shaykh:** Carving, if it is established, is possible. They would carry the mountain. Where was their location?

﴿And mention the brother of 'Ad, when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾ [al-Ahqaf 21]. It is well known that al-Ahqaf are all sandy hills. But in any case, whether this example is authentic or not, they were without doubt strong and mighty, so they said: ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, replied to them: ﴿Did they not see﴾, meaning did they not know, ﴿that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength﴾ [Fussilat 15]. This is an affirmation that Allah, the Exalted, is mightier than them in strength. ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them﴾. He did not say "that Allah is mightier" but said ﴿who created them﴾, to show their weakness, that they are created, and that the Creator will be stronger than them. So the One who created them is mightier than them in strength, because He is the One who gave them strength, and the Giver of perfection is more deserving of it. This is the wisdom behind His, the Exalted's, saying ﴿that Allah, who created them﴾, and not saying "Did they not know that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth," or "that Allah is mightier than them in strength." It is to show their weakness and that they are created and weak.

He said: ﴿And they were denying Our signs﴾ [Fussilat 15]. The saying ﴿And they were denying Our signs﴾ is coordinated with His saying ﴿they were arrogant in the land﴾ and ﴿and said﴾ [Fussilat 15]: ﴿and they were denying Our signs﴾. He said: (Our signs: the miracles). ﴿Denying﴾ means they rejected, because jaḥd is rejection and denial, especially since it is followed by the preposition bi (with), which indicates that. The author's saying "Our signs: Our miracles" is open to review, because the signs (āyāt) are the indications and evidences pointing to the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, and they are not merely miracles. We have mentioned that miracles can be signs, and that some can come from devils through sorcerers and otherwise. But when we say "signs", its meaning becomes indicators showing the truth: ﴿and they were denying Our signs﴾.

(﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind﴾ [Fussilat 16]: cold, of intense sound, without rain.) ﴿A wind﴾ here is indefinite, intended for magnification, meaning a great wind. ﴿Furious﴾ means of intense sound; you hear from it a sound like thunder because of its intensity and the violence of its collision with the air, the trees, the stones, and the houses.

The author's saying "without rain" — it seems apparent that the present context does not indicate this in this verse, as it appears to me. But the saying of Allah, the Exalted, has indicated it: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾ [al-Dhariyat 41], meaning one that carries no rain, because rain is one of the causes of winds. Allah, the Exalted, sends them, and they stir up clouds, and He spreads them in the sky however He wills, makes them fragments, and you see the rain coming out from among them. But the wind of 'Ad had none of that.

(﴿In days of ill omen﴾ [Fussilat 16]: with a kasra or sukūn on the ḥā', unlucky for them.) ﴿In days﴾: Allah defined the length of these days in another verse, when He said: ﴿seven nights and eight days in succession﴾ [al-Haqqah 7]. Did it begin at dawn and end with it, or at sunset? It began at dawn and ends... let us see: first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh: seven nights and eight days. Eight days end at sunset, and seven nights because the first night was omitted.

He, may He be exalted, says: (﴿That We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace﴾, meaning humiliation, ﴿in the life of this world﴾). The lām here indicates outcome, and it may also indicate causation; both are correct. Allah sent upon them the barren wind for this purpose, or He sent upon them the barren wind so that their outcome was that they tasted the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. This is the life we live, and it was called "dunyā" (the worldly life) for two reasons: because of its lowliness and insignificance compared to the Hereafter, since the place of a person's whip in Paradise is better than this world and what is in it; and also because it is a troubled world, where hardly a month passes without you finding some disturbance, or even less, as the poet said:

*One day for us and one day against us,
one day we are grieved, and one day we rejoice.*

The second reason: because it is near (dānī), since it precedes the Hereafter, so it is nearer to created beings than the Hereafter. So why was it called dunyā?

* **Student:** Either because of its lowliness or its insignificance, or (...), or — because it, along with lowliness, is full of many disturbances and is not like the Hereafter; or because it is near and close.

* **Shaykh:** Yes, as Allah said: ﴿its fruits are near﴾ [al-Haqqah 23], meaning close. And Usama's saying "either for this or for that" is wrong; the correct statement is "for this and that," because it combines both matters; it is not "either this or that."

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing﴾ [Fussilat 16], meaning more severe, ﴿and they will not be helped﴾ [Fussilat 16], by having it prevented from them. The lām in His saying ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter﴾ is called the lām al-ibtidā' (initial lām), and it is for emphasis. Therefore, when inna (indeed) comes, where does the lām go? It is shifted (zuḥlika), delayed from its place, and it appears in the later part of the subject of inna or its predicate. We shifted it so that two consecutive emphasizing elements would not gather at the beginning of the sentence. Therefore we say: the lām in His saying ﴿And the punishment﴾ is the lām al-ibtidā' and conveys emphasis, and what supports this is that with inna it is shifted away from it. ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing﴾, meaning more severe in humiliation — may Allah protect us — because the punishment of this world is not heard of by those who came before, is it not so?

* **Students:** Yes.

* **Shaykh:** And it is not seen by those who came after, is it not so?

* **Students:** Yes.

* **Shaykh:** It is not heard of by those who came before, because it came after them. So the peoples before 'Ad did not know of it, and the peoples after them did not see it; they heard of it but did not see it. But in the Hereafter there is both hearing and seeing — may Allah protect us — the one who is punished in the Hereafter is seen and heard by everyone, the earlier and the later. Therefore He said: ﴿more disgracing﴾. Then it is also more severe, as Allah said in another verse: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾ [Ta-Ha 127], more severe and greater, as you know, of the punishment of the Fire. May Allah protect us and you from it.

﴿And they will not be helped﴾ [Fussilat 16]: this is a resumptive sentence (isti'nāf), meaning that in the Hereafter no one will help them. In this world, a person may be helped against punishment, by repelling it or lifting it: by repelling it before it occurs, or lifting it after it occurs. But in the Hereafter there is no helper.

* In these verses are benefits, among them: the explanation of the enormity of the arrogance of these deniers toward their prophet, namely 'Ad, by His saying: ﴿So they were arrogant in the land without right and said, "Who is mightier than us in strength?"﴾ [Fussilat 15].

* Among them: the explanation of human transgression, and that man has no limit to his transgression, because reaching this level, ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾, indicates great transgression and pride.

* Among them: the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in punishing them, for they were seized with what is among the gentlest things: the gentle wind by which the body is revived, strengthened, and energized. It is with this wind that 'Ad were destroyed, because they said: ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾. And look at Pharaoh when he said: ﴿Is not mine the kingdom of Egypt, and these rivers flow beneath me? Do you not see? (51) Or am I better than this one who is despised and can hardly express himself?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 51–52]. With what was he punished? With the water that he had prided himself on the day before.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the eloquence of the Qur'an in persuasion and establishing proof, by His saying: ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 15]. The aspect of that is that He said: ﴿who created them﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of making a comparison between the Creator and the created, by His saying: ﴿mightier than them in strength﴾, although He, glorified and exalted, is mightier than everyone. But the context is one of argument, and in a context of argument there is no harm in mentioning a comparison between the one preferred and the one it is compared with. A parallel to this, indeed even more eloquent than it, is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ [al-Naml 59]. Tell me: is there any good in their idols?

* **Student:** No.

* **Shaykh:** But this is part of the mode of argument, where a person argues against the opponent with what the opponent acknowledges.

But the context is one of argument, and in a context of argument there is no harm in mentioning a comparison between the one preferred and the one it is compared with. A parallel to this, indeed even more eloquent than it, is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ [al-Naml 59]. Tell me: is there any good in their idols?

* **Students:** No.

* **Shaykh:** But this is part of the mode of argument, where a person argues against the opponent with what he acknowledges.

His saying ﴿He is mightier than them in strength﴾ [Fussilat 15] leads to the following benefits: the error of one who interprets the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am 124], ﴿And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Isra' 55], ﴿And He knows best those who are guided﴾ [al-An'am 117], and similar verses, by interpreting "a'lam" (knows best) as "ʿālim" (knowing), like the Jalalayn (the tafsir of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti), may Allah have mercy on them both.

"A'lam" — saying "ʿālim" is a grave error and a distortion of the Qur'an. Which is more eloquent: a'lam or ʿālim?

* **Students:** A'lam.

* **Shaykh:** A'lam, because a'lam excludes sharing, whereas ʿālim does not exclude sharing. You say: "So-and-so is knowing (ʿālim), and so-and-so is knowing, and so-and-so is knowing." But if you say: "So-and-so is more knowing (a'lam)," it means that no one equals him in rank. So interpreting "a'lam" as "ʿālim" is without doubt a distortion of the Qur'an and a great deficiency.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the explanation that these deniers of Hud, namely 'Ad, combined two things: arrogance and denial. Arrogance is in His saying ﴿So they were arrogant in the land﴾, and denial in ﴿and they were denying Our signs﴾ [Fussilat 15].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent the messengers with signs and established clear proofs and evidences that He is the Truth, and that His messengers are true, by His saying: ﴿Our signs﴾.

* Among the benefits of these verses: that the winds flow by the command of Allah, by His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾ [Fussilat 16]. There is no doubt that everything proceeds by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, even the actions of human beings occur by the command of Allah, as is the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah (the people of the Sunnah and the community). Everything moves by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: the winds, the clouds, the seas, and the rivers all flow by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the explanation of the condition of this wind by which Allah destroyed 'Ad, and that it was a furious, intense wind. In other verses there is what indicates that it had no rain and no good in it; rather it was barren of all good.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in recompensing those who deserve recompense, in that they are repaid with the like of their deeds. For this reason the scholars say: "Recompense is of the same kind as the deed." The aspect of that is that Allah sent upon these arrogant people, who say "Who is mightier than us in strength?", the soft, gentle wind. Among the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in this punishment is that it did not sweep them away all at once, but was imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days, so that the continuation of the punishment would be more severe. For a punished person, if he were punished with something that destroyed him immediately, he would be finished with the punishment; but if the punishment comes upon him over hours or days, it becomes more severe.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the explanation that the actions of Allah, the Exalted, are accompanied by wisdom, by His saying: ﴿that We might make them taste﴾ [Fussilat 16]. This is the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah: that the actions of Allah, the Exalted, are accompanied by wisdom, and that His legislation is accompanied by wisdom. Whatever He legislates or decrees, it is for a wisdom. But is this wisdom known? Some of it is known, and some of it is not known.

Give me an example of something whose wisdom is not comprehensible, meaning we cannot grasp it by reason.

* **Student:** That is, something the mind cannot grasp.

* **Shaykh:** Among the matters of the Sharia (legislation) or of the divine decree there are things whose wisdom is known, and there are things whose wisdom is not known. I want you to give me an example of the things whose wisdom we do not know.

* **Student:** You mean from the decreed matters?

* **Shaykh:** No, from the legislated matters; that is easier for you.

* **Student:** From the legislated matters, meaning like what the disbelievers are punished with...

* **Shaykh:** No, that is a known wisdom.

* **Student:** The obligation of the five daily prayers.

Shaykh: Yes. Like the five daily prayers, we do not know the wisdom in their being five, nor do we know the wisdom in their being four, four, four, two, and three. We do not know it, because our minds are limited. But we know that Allah does nothing except for a wisdom. This is why 'Aishah, when Mu'adhah asked her, said: "We used to experience that [menstruation], and we were commanded to make up the fast, and we were not commanded to make up the prayer" [narrated by Muslim (335/69) from the hadith of 'Aishah]. That is, if the matter is so, that we are commanded to make up this and not that, then this must be for a wisdom.

Now, among the scholars of the Ummah and its sects are those who say: the actions of Allah are not caused by any reason, they have no wisdom, and His legislation has no wisdom; He acts merely by His will and judges by the Shari'ah merely by His will. These people have, without doubt, attributed to Allah deficiency and foolishness. Allah has denounced this in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ [Sad 27], and He said: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play﴾ [ad-Dukhan 38], and He said: ﴿Did you suppose that We created you uselessly and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 115]. The verses on this are many, and every verse containing the lam of causation (al-lam al-ta'lil) indicates wisdom.

Now, there are people who went to the opposite extreme and said: the actions of Allah are caused by wisdom, and it is obligatory upon Him to do what wisdom requires, and to legislate what wisdom requires. These people were correct in one respect and mistaken in another. They were correct in that they thought we impose upon our Lord, by our minds, what we see wisdom requires. Is this wrong or right?

These people say: it is obligatory upon Allah to do what contains wisdom, as an obligation. This is wrong in one respect and right in another. If they mean by this that we impose upon Allah to do what our minds judge to be wisdom, then this is wrong. But if they mean that Allah has made it obligatory upon Himself to do what contains wisdom, because He is Wise, then this is correct. We have no doubt that wisdom is the intent of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that He does nothing and judges nothing except for a wisdom. But is it we who determine the wisdom and then impose upon Allah that He must act? This is the error. The second view is the position of the Mu'tazilah, and the first is the position of the Ash'ariyyah and their followers. The correct position is the middle way, and the best of matters is always the middle.

* A student: What is the middle way, O Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: The middle way is that Allah has made it obligatory upon Himself to act, by His own imposition of wisdom, because He negated that His actions are in vain, or playful, or false. This implies that He, glorified and exalted, does a thing for a wisdom. But it is not us who impose it upon Allah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe than the punishment of this world, from His saying: ﴿that He may make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world﴾.

* And among its benefits: the disbeliever is punished with two punishments: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, from His saying: ﴿that He may make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing﴾.

As for the believer, Allah, exalted is He, does not combine two punishments upon him. If he is punished for a sin in this world, he is not punished for it in the Hereafter, because of the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is by what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [ash-Shura 30], and because the Prophet (ﷺ) informed that whoever commits any of these filthy things, meaning the sins, and is punished for it in this world, will not be punished for it in the Hereafter.

So the believer, if he is punished in this world for his deed, will not be punished for it in the Hereafter, whereas the disbeliever is punished with this and with that. Consider His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse—and whoever does that will meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Furqan 68-69], where He said: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him﴾. Either the meaning is that the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe, so it is doubled in relation to its severity, or it is that he is gathered for him between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

Our saying that he is gathered for him between two punishments does not mean that this is inevitable. Rather we say: if he is punished for his sin in this world, he is not safe from being punished for it in the Hereafter. Pay attention to this, lest it be objected to us that the disbelievers now die while in the utmost state of joy, health, wealth and children, and find no punishment.

The meaning is that they do not find a punishment that is witnessed. But the punishment of the heart is certainly present for them. The people most punished in heart and most anxious are the disbelievers, and the more a person disobeys his Lord, the more anxious and the less at ease he is; and the more he has faith and does righteous deeds, the more tranquil he is. Listen to His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them with their best of what they used to do﴾ [an-Nahl 97]. He did not say, Mighty and Majestic: "We will surely give him much wealth." No; "We will cause him to live a good life," even if he is poor. So you find his life good, his mind at peace, at rest, concerned with nothing except what pleases Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there is no helper for the punished on the Day of Resurrection, from His saying: ﴿and they will not be helped﴾. And there are witnesses for this, among them His saying: ﴿On the Day when secrets are examined, he will have no power and no helper﴾ [at-Tariq 9-10]. Likewise, they will acknowledge: ﴿So we have no intercessors, and no close friend﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 100-101].

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿So as for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right, and said, "Who is mightier than us in strength?" Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they were denying Our signs.﴾ (15) ﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind in days of ill omen, that We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.﴾ [Fussilat 15–16].

* **Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, said, when He mentioned the command to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to warn the Quraysh with a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud, that He would explain what happened to 'Ad and what happened to Thamud. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So as for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right.﴾ The word (ammā, "as for") is a conditional and distinguishing particle. As for its being a conditional particle, it is because it has a condition and a response: ﴿So as for 'Ad, they were arrogant﴾. As for its being a distinguishing particle, it is because it comes in that sense too: ﴿As for him who gives and fears (Allah) (5), and believes in the best reward﴾ [al-Layl 5–6], and ﴿As for him who is miserly and considers himself self-sufficient (8), and denies the best reward﴾ [al-Layl 8–9]. So it is a particle of condition and distinction.

﴿So as for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right.﴾ "Istakbarū" means: pride overtook them. The sīn and tā' were added for emphasis, meaning they became exceedingly proud.

His saying ﴿without right﴾ is not a restrictive qualifier but a clarifying qualifier, because every arrogance in the land is without right. Arrogance does not divide into two kinds; it is one kind, so every arrogance is without right. Such a qualifier is called a clarifying qualifier (ṣifah kāshifah), meaning it reveals what came before and shows its reality. So what is the reality of arrogance? That it is without right. Right is the opposite of falsehood, and falsehood is either in a statement or in a demand. Falsehood in a statement is lying, and falsehood in judgment is injustice. The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿and that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood﴾ [al-Hajj 62] includes both matters: it includes their claim that these are gods, which is a false claim, and it includes their act of worshipping these gods, which is injustice and wrongdoing, since they equate the created with the Creator.

﴿And they said﴾, meaning as part of what they were arrogant about. (﴿They said﴾ when they were warned of punishment: ﴿"Who is mightier than us in strength?"﴾) meaning: no one. The interrogative ﴿man﴾ here carries the sense of negation and denial. We have repeatedly mentioned that when the interrogative has the meaning of denial and negation, it becomes more emphatic than plain negation, because it contains a challenge.

﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ As you know, ﴿man﴾ is an interrogative noun, ﴿ashaddu﴾ is the predicate of the subject, because ﴿man﴾ is the subject and ﴿ashaddu﴾ is its predicate, and ﴿quwwatan﴾ is a specifying accusative (tamyīz) for ﴿ashaddu﴾. Among the general rules is that when a noun in the accusative comes after a comparative form, it is a tamyīz. ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ means no one.

Then the author mentioned an example of their strength. He said: (Each one of them would uproot a huge rock from the mountain and place it wherever he wished.) This example may be true, or it may be from the Isra'iliyyat (narrations from Israelite sources), because it is known that 'Ad were what?

* **Student:** They carved.

* **Shaykh:** Carving, if it is established, is possible. They would carry the mountain. Where was their location?

﴿And mention the brother of 'Ad, when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾ [al-Ahqaf 21]. It is well known that al-Ahqaf are all sandy hills. But in any case, whether this example is authentic or not, they were without doubt strong and mighty, so they said: ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, replied to them: ﴿Did they not see﴾, meaning did they not know, ﴿that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength﴾ [Fussilat 15]. This is an affirmation that Allah, the Exalted, is mightier than them in strength. ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them﴾. He did not say "that Allah is mightier" but said ﴿who created them﴾, to show their weakness, that they are created, and that the Creator will be stronger than them. So the One who created them is mightier than them in strength, because He is the One who gave them strength, and the Giver of perfection is more deserving of it. This is the wisdom behind His, the Exalted's, saying ﴿that Allah, who created them﴾, and not saying "Did they not know that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth," or "that Allah is mightier than them in strength." It is to show their weakness and that they are created and weak.

He said: ﴿And they were denying Our signs﴾ [Fussilat 15]. The saying ﴿And they were denying Our signs﴾ is coordinated with His saying ﴿they were arrogant in the land﴾ and ﴿and said﴾ [Fussilat 15]: ﴿and they were denying Our signs﴾. He said: (Our signs: the miracles). ﴿Denying﴾ means they rejected, because jaḥd is rejection and denial, especially since it is followed by the preposition bi (with), which indicates that. The author's saying "Our signs: Our miracles" is open to review, because the signs (āyāt) are the indications and evidences pointing to the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, and they are not merely miracles. We have mentioned that miracles can be signs, and that some can come from devils through sorcerers and otherwise. But when we say "signs", its meaning becomes indicators showing the truth: ﴿and they were denying Our signs﴾.

(﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind﴾ [Fussilat 16]: cold, of intense sound, without rain.) ﴿A wind﴾ here is indefinite, intended for magnification, meaning a great wind. ﴿Furious﴾ means of intense sound; you hear from it a sound like thunder because of its intensity and the violence of its collision with the air, the trees, the stones, and the houses.

The author's saying "without rain" — it seems apparent that the present context does not indicate this in this verse, as it appears to me. But the saying of Allah, the Exalted, has indicated it: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾ [al-Dhariyat 41], meaning one that carries no rain, because rain is one of the causes of winds. Allah, the Exalted, sends them, and they stir up clouds, and He spreads them in the sky however He wills, makes them fragments, and you see the rain coming out from among them. But the wind of 'Ad had none of that.

(﴿In days of ill omen﴾ [Fussilat 16]: with a kasra or sukūn on the ḥā', unlucky for them.) ﴿In days﴾: Allah defined the length of these days in another verse, when He said: ﴿seven nights and eight days in succession﴾ [al-Haqqah 7]. Did it begin at dawn and end with it, or at sunset? It began at dawn and ends... let us see: first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh: seven nights and eight days. Eight days end at sunset, and seven nights because the first night was omitted.

He, may He be exalted, says: (﴿That We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace﴾, meaning humiliation, ﴿in the life of this world﴾). The lām here indicates outcome, and it may also indicate causation; both are correct. Allah sent upon them the barren wind for this purpose, or He sent upon them the barren wind so that their outcome was that they tasted the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. This is the life we live, and it was called "dunyā" (the worldly life) for two reasons: because of its lowliness and insignificance compared to the Hereafter, since the place of a person's whip in Paradise is better than this world and what is in it; and also because it is a troubled world, where hardly a month passes without you finding some disturbance, or even less, as the poet said:

*One day for us and one day against us,
one day we are grieved, and one day we rejoice.*

The second reason: because it is near (dānī), since it precedes the Hereafter, so it is nearer to created beings than the Hereafter. So why was it called dunyā?

* **Student:** Either because of its lowliness or its insignificance, or (...), or — because it, along with lowliness, is full of many disturbances and is not like the Hereafter; or because it is near and close.

* **Shaykh:** Yes, as Allah said: ﴿its fruits are near﴾ [al-Haqqah 23], meaning close. And Usama's saying "either for this or for that" is wrong; the correct statement is "for this and that," because it combines both matters; it is not "either this or that."

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing﴾ [Fussilat 16], meaning more severe, ﴿and they will not be helped﴾ [Fussilat 16], by having it prevented from them. The lām in His saying ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter﴾ is called the lām al-ibtidā' (initial lām), and it is for emphasis. Therefore, when inna (indeed) comes, where does the lām go? It is shifted (zuḥlika), delayed from its place, and it appears in the later part of the subject of inna or its predicate. We shifted it so that two consecutive emphasizing elements would not gather at the beginning of the sentence. Therefore we say: the lām in His saying ﴿And the punishment﴾ is the lām al-ibtidā' and conveys emphasis, and what supports this is that with inna it is shifted away from it. ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing﴾, meaning more severe in humiliation — may Allah protect us — because the punishment of this world is not heard of by those who came before, is it not so?

* **Students:** Yes.

* **Shaykh:** And it is not seen by those who came after, is it not so?

* **Students:** Yes.

* **Shaykh:** It is not heard of by those who came before, because it came after them. So the peoples before 'Ad did not know of it, and the peoples after them did not see it; they heard of it but did not see it. But in the Hereafter there is both hearing and seeing — may Allah protect us — the one who is punished in the Hereafter is seen and heard by everyone, the earlier and the later. Therefore He said: ﴿more disgracing﴾. Then it is also more severe, as Allah said in another verse: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾ [Ta-Ha 127], more severe and greater, as you know, of the punishment of the Fire. May Allah protect us and you from it.

﴿And they will not be helped﴾ [Fussilat 16]: this is a resumptive sentence (isti'nāf), meaning that in the Hereafter no one will help them. In this world, a person may be helped against punishment, by repelling it or lifting it: by repelling it before it occurs, or lifting it after it occurs. But in the Hereafter there is no helper.

* In these verses are benefits, among them: the explanation of the enormity of the arrogance of these deniers toward their prophet, namely 'Ad, by His saying: ﴿So they were arrogant in the land without right and said, "Who is mightier than us in strength?"﴾ [Fussilat 15].

* Among them: the explanation of human transgression, and that man has no limit to his transgression, because reaching this level, ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾, indicates great transgression and pride.

* Among them: the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in punishing them, for they were seized with what is among the gentlest things: the gentle wind by which the body is revived, strengthened, and energized. It is with this wind that 'Ad were destroyed, because they said: ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾. And look at Pharaoh when he said: ﴿Is not mine the kingdom of Egypt, and these rivers flow beneath me? Do you not see? (51) Or am I better than this one who is despised and can hardly express himself?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 51–52]. With what was he punished? With the water that he had prided himself on the day before.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the eloquence of the Qur'an in persuasion and establishing proof, by His saying: ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 15]. The aspect of that is that He said: ﴿who created them﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of making a comparison between the Creator and the created, by His saying: ﴿mightier than them in strength﴾, although He, glorified and exalted, is mightier than everyone. But the context is one of argument, and in a context of argument there is no harm in mentioning a comparison between the one preferred and the one it is compared with. A parallel to this, indeed even more eloquent than it, is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ [al-Naml 59]. Tell me: is there any good in their idols?

* **Student:** No.

* **Shaykh:** But this is part of the mode of argument, where a person argues against the opponent with what the opponent acknowledges.

But the context is one of argument, and in a context of argument there is no harm in mentioning a comparison between the one preferred and the one it is compared with. A parallel to this, indeed even more eloquent than it, is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ [al-Naml 59]. Tell me: is there any good in their idols?

* **Students:** No.

* **Shaykh:** But this is part of the mode of argument, where a person argues against the opponent with what he acknowledges.

His saying ﴿He is mightier than them in strength﴾ [Fussilat 15] leads to the following benefits: the error of one who interprets the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am 124], ﴿And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Isra' 55], ﴿And He knows best those who are guided﴾ [al-An'am 117], and similar verses, by interpreting "a'lam" (knows best) as "ʿālim" (knowing), like the Jalalayn (the tafsir of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti), may Allah have mercy on them both.

"A'lam" — saying "ʿālim" is a grave error and a distortion of the Qur'an. Which is more eloquent: a'lam or ʿālim?

* **Students:** A'lam.

* **Shaykh:** A'lam, because a'lam excludes sharing, whereas ʿālim does not exclude sharing. You say: "So-and-so is knowing (ʿālim), and so-and-so is knowing, and so-and-so is knowing." But if you say: "So-and-so is more knowing (a'lam)," it means that no one equals him in rank. So interpreting "a'lam" as "ʿālim" is without doubt a distortion of the Qur'an and a great deficiency.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the explanation that these deniers of Hud, namely 'Ad, combined two things: arrogance and denial. Arrogance is in His saying ﴿So they were arrogant in the land﴾, and denial in ﴿and they were denying Our signs﴾ [Fussilat 15].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent the messengers with signs and established clear proofs and evidences that He is the Truth, and that His messengers are true, by His saying: ﴿Our signs﴾.

* Among the benefits of these verses: that the winds flow by the command of Allah, by His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾ [Fussilat 16]. There is no doubt that everything proceeds by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, even the actions of human beings occur by the command of Allah, as is the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah (the people of the Sunnah and the community). Everything moves by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: the winds, the clouds, the seas, and the rivers all flow by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the explanation of the condition of this wind by which Allah destroyed 'Ad, and that it was a furious, intense wind. In other verses there is what indicates that it had no rain and no good in it; rather it was barren of all good.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in recompensing those who deserve recompense, in that they are repaid with the like of their deeds. For this reason the scholars say: "Recompense is of the same kind as the deed." The aspect of that is that Allah sent upon these arrogant people, who say "Who is mightier than us in strength?", the soft, gentle wind. Among the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in this punishment is that it did not sweep them away all at once, but was imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days, so that the continuation of the punishment would be more severe. For a punished person, if he were punished with something that destroyed him immediately, he would be finished with the punishment; but if the punishment comes upon him over hours or days, it becomes more severe.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the explanation that the actions of Allah, the Exalted, are accompanied by wisdom, by His saying: ﴿that We might make them taste﴾ [Fussilat 16]. This is the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah: that the actions of Allah, the Exalted, are accompanied by wisdom, and that His legislation is accompanied by wisdom. Whatever He legislates or decrees, it is for a wisdom. But is this wisdom known? Some of it is known, and some of it is not known.

Give me an example of something whose wisdom is not comprehensible, meaning we cannot grasp it by reason.

* **Student:** That is, something the mind cannot grasp.

* **Shaykh:** Among the matters of the Sharia (legislation) or of the divine decree there are things whose wisdom is known, and there are things whose wisdom is not known. I want you to give me an example of the things whose wisdom we do not know.

* **Student:** You mean from the decreed matters?

* **Shaykh:** No, from the legislated matters; that is easier for you.

* **Student:** From the legislated matters, meaning like what the disbelievers are punished with...

* **Shaykh:** No, that is a known wisdom.

* **Student:** The obligation of the five daily prayers.

Shaykh: Yes. Like the five daily prayers, we do not know the wisdom in their being five, nor do we know the wisdom in their being four, four, four, two, and three. We do not know it, because our minds are limited. But we know that Allah does nothing except for a wisdom. This is why 'Aishah, when Mu'adhah asked her, said: "We used to experience that [menstruation], and we were commanded to make up the fast, and we were not commanded to make up the prayer" [narrated by Muslim (335/69) from the hadith of 'Aishah]. That is, if the matter is so, that we are commanded to make up this and not that, then this must be for a wisdom.

Now, among the scholars of the Ummah and its sects are those who say: the actions of Allah are not caused by any reason, they have no wisdom, and His legislation has no wisdom; He acts merely by His will and judges by the Shari'ah merely by His will. These people have, without doubt, attributed to Allah deficiency and foolishness. Allah has denounced this in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ [Sad 27], and He said: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play﴾ [ad-Dukhan 38], and He said: ﴿Did you suppose that We created you uselessly and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 115]. The verses on this are many, and every verse containing the lam of causation (al-lam al-ta'lil) indicates wisdom.

Now, there are people who went to the opposite extreme and said: the actions of Allah are caused by wisdom, and it is obligatory upon Him to do what wisdom requires, and to legislate what wisdom requires. These people were correct in one respect and mistaken in another. They were correct in that they thought we impose upon our Lord, by our minds, what we see wisdom requires. Is this wrong or right?

These people say: it is obligatory upon Allah to do what contains wisdom, as an obligation. This is wrong in one respect and right in another. If they mean by this that we impose upon Allah to do what our minds judge to be wisdom, then this is wrong. But if they mean that Allah has made it obligatory upon Himself to do what contains wisdom, because He is Wise, then this is correct. We have no doubt that wisdom is the intent of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that He does nothing and judges nothing except for a wisdom. But is it we who determine the wisdom and then impose upon Allah that He must act? This is the error. The second view is the position of the Mu'tazilah, and the first is the position of the Ash'ariyyah and their followers. The correct position is the middle way, and the best of matters is always the middle.

* A student: What is the middle way, O Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: The middle way is that Allah has made it obligatory upon Himself to act, by His own imposition of wisdom, because He negated that His actions are in vain, or playful, or false. This implies that He, glorified and exalted, does a thing for a wisdom. But it is not us who impose it upon Allah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe than the punishment of this world, from His saying: ﴿that He may make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world﴾.

* And among its benefits: the disbeliever is punished with two punishments: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, from His saying: ﴿that He may make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing﴾.

As for the believer, Allah, exalted is He, does not combine two punishments upon him. If he is punished for a sin in this world, he is not punished for it in the Hereafter, because of the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is by what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [ash-Shura 30], and because the Prophet (ﷺ) informed that whoever commits any of these filthy things, meaning the sins, and is punished for it in this world, will not be punished for it in the Hereafter.

So the believer, if he is punished in this world for his deed, will not be punished for it in the Hereafter, whereas the disbeliever is punished with this and with that. Consider His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse—and whoever does that will meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Furqan 68-69], where He said: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him﴾. Either the meaning is that the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe, so it is doubled in relation to its severity, or it is that he is gathered for him between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

Our saying that he is gathered for him between two punishments does not mean that this is inevitable. Rather we say: if he is punished for his sin in this world, he is not safe from being punished for it in the Hereafter. Pay attention to this, lest it be objected to us that the disbelievers now die while in the utmost state of joy, health, wealth and children, and find no punishment.

The meaning is that they do not find a punishment that is witnessed. But the punishment of the heart is certainly present for them. The people most punished in heart and most anxious are the disbelievers, and the more a person disobeys his Lord, the more anxious and the less at ease he is; and the more he has faith and does righteous deeds, the more tranquil he is. Listen to His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them with their best of what they used to do﴾ [an-Nahl 97]. He did not say, Mighty and Majestic: "We will surely give him much wealth." No; "We will cause him to live a good life," even if he is poor. So you find his life good, his mind at peace, at rest, concerned with nothing except what pleases Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there is no helper for the punished on the Day of Resurrection, from His saying: ﴿and they will not be helped﴾. And there are witnesses for this, among them His saying: ﴿On the Day when secrets are examined, he will have no power and no helper﴾ [at-Tariq 9-10]. Likewise, they will acknowledge: ﴿So we have no intercessors, and no close friend﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 100-101].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 41, verses 17–18 (part 1 of 2):

Then He said: ﴿And as for them, they will not be helped.﴾

As for the second division, He said: (﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them﴾ [Fussilat 17]: We made the path of guidance clear to them.)

﴿Thamud⌋ is without tanwin (nunation), and ﴿'Ad⌋ is with tanwin. So why?

Student: It is mamnu' min al-sarf (diptote, a noun that does not take full declension).

Shaykh: Which of them?

Student: Thamud.

Shaykh: Because Thamud is mamnu' min al-sarf. And 'Ad?

Student: It is not mamnu' min al-sarf.

Shaykh: It is not mamnu' min al-sarf. And what is al-sarf (full declension)? Is al-sarf the genitive of what is not declinable marked with a fatha, or is al-sarf something else?

Student: It is the absence of tanwin.

Shaykh: The absence of tanwin. Ibn Malik said:

*Al-sarf is the tanwin that comes to make clear a meaning, by which the noun becomes fully declinable.*

That is al-sarf.

﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them﴾. The commentator said: (We made the path of guidance clear to them). So the guidance here is guidance by clarification; that is, the truth was made clear to them. Know that everyone who disbelieves, disbelieves after the truth has become clear to him when the Messenger comes to him, because the Messengers, peace and blessings be upon them, make the truth clear. They do not leave anything that needs clarification without clarifying it.

He said here: ﴿We guided them﴾, meaning: We made the path of truth clear to them. So the guidance here is guidance of clarification and direction.

(﴿But they preferred blindness﴾ chose disbelief ﴿over guidance﴾): meaning the guidance of divine enabling (tawfiq); that is, over being guided. They preferred blindness, which is disbelief, over guidance, which is Islam.

﴿So the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn﴾ [Fussilat 17].

﴿The thunderbolt of the punishment seized them﴾, meaning the punishment of the thunderbolt, because Thamud were shouted at and shaken, and they were struck down (ṣa'iqu). They were destroyed with the destruction of one man. They were found in their homes, prostrate on their knees, lifeless, may God protect us.

His saying: ﴿the humiliating punishment﴾ means the degrading punishment, because al-hawn means humiliation.

﴿For what they used to earn﴾: the bi' indicates causation, and ma may be a relative pronoun, in which case its returning pronoun is omitted, the sense being: "for what they used to earn." Or it may be a verbal (masdariyya) particle, in which case it needs no returning pronoun, and the sense is: "for their earning."

(﴿And We saved﴾ from it) meaning from the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment ﴿those who believed and used to be mindful of God﴾ [Fussilat 18]: We saved from this punishment those who believed and were mindful of God. They combined faith and piety, and this is the cause of salvation. God willing, the explanation of what may be derived from the verses will come later.

Student: We have said that when a believer is punished in this world, God does not combine the punishment of the Hereafter for him. Does this include even someone who was punished without repenting, while persisting in his sin, such as an adulterer, for example?

Shaykh: Yes, because if he repents he is not punished, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

Student: O Shaykh, the one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin. The opposite would be that he is like one who still has a sin, because he did not benefit from this punishment and was not restrained?

Shaykh: If he is punished, the sin of what preceded is erased from him, because he has received his recompense and it is over. But the punishment may be deferred for him until the Day of Resurrection. That is why, when God loves a people, He hastens their punishment in this world, so that they are not disgraced by it on the Day of Resurrection.

Student: O Shaykh, if he is punished now and then dies immediately, before committing another sin, is he punished for the intention of not repenting?

Shaykh: No. He is punished if the intention persists after the punishment. This is perhaps punished for his intention, not for his action.

Student: O Shaykh, may God be good to you, the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And as for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land﴾. And in the hadith: "No one who has in his heart an atom's weight of pride will enter Paradise" [[Narrated by Muslim (91 / 147) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]]. Does this mean he will not enter Paradise at first entry, or that he will never enter Paradise?

Shaykh: No. This has a distinction. If the pride is disbelief, then he will never enter Paradise. If it is pride along with faith, then he will not enter it with unconditional entry that is not preceded by punishment. This is also among the verses of warning: if God wills, He pardons it. ﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa' 48].

Student: Is his saying ﴿they were arrogant in the land without right﴾ like His saying: ﴿and sin and oppression without right﴾ [Al-A'raf 33]?

Shaykh: Yes, it is like it. This is a clarifying attribute.

Student: May God be good to you. Is the punishment of the disbelievers, that is, once they die, continuous until the Day of Resurrection, or will they be punished in this world on the Day of Resurrection?

Shaykh: Say: "Is it the punishment of the grave." May God bless you.

As for the punishment of the disbelievers in the Hereafter, it is continuous. But the punishment of the grave, as for the believer, may be cut off: he is punished according to his sins and then it ends. As for the disbeliever, the apparent meaning is that it continues.

Student: The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿In days of ill omen﴾, the attribution of ill omen (nahs) to days.

Shaykh: Yes, there is no harm in it, as Lot said: ﴿This is a distressful day﴾ [Hud 77]. This is when the intention is merely information. Here the intention is merely information. But if the intention is to find fault and insult, it is not permitted. So this insult or fault-finding is either by way of reporting or by way of insult. The first is permitted; the second is not permitted. A parallel to this is the sick person reporting what he feels. Sometimes his companion asks him, "How are you last night?" and he complains, saying: "By God, I did not sleep last night, pains in the head, in the neck, in the back, in the stomach, in the legs." If he says this by way of complaining, this is not permitted, because it contradicts patience. If he says it by way of reporting, there is no harm in it. That is why some sick people say, introducing it: "Reporting, not complaining: such and such happened to me." Do you understand?

Student: May God bless you. The one who is punished for his intention, is he punished if he does not carry out the act?

Shaykh: No. The punishment is for the intention. If a person intends to commit a sin, either he resists this intention and abandons the sin for the sake of the Mighty and Majestic, and he is rewarded for this; or he persists in his intention and resolves, but he is unable to do it, and he is punished for his intention.

* * *

Student: I seek refuge with God from the accursed Satan. ﴿And on the Day when the enemies of God are gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in ranks. Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their eyes, and their skins will testify against them concerning what they used to do. And they will say to their skins: "Why did you testify against us?" They will say: "God has made us speak, who makes everything speak, and He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned. And you did not conceal yourselves so that your hearing or your eyes or your skins would testify against you, but you thought that God does not know much of what you do. And that is your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers.
