Then the Most High said: ﴿So if they are arrogant﴾ [Fussilat 38], meaning: from worshipping Allah and prostrating to Him. Allah, the Most High, is free of need of them (﴿so if they are arrogant﴾ from prostrating to Allah alone, ﴿then those who are with your Lord﴾, i.e., the angels, ﴿glorify Him﴾ pray ﴿for Him night and day, and they never tire﴾ they do not grow weary). The meaning: if these people are arrogant towards worshipping Allah, then Allah has other servants, as in His words: ﴿If they disbelieve in it, then We have entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it﴾ [al-An'am 89]. Then, on the assumption that there is no worshipper of Allah at all, Allah says: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need of you﴾ [al-Zumar 7], and ﴿Whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need of the worlds﴾ [Al 'Imran 97]. So here there are two matters:
The first: that a group of created beings is arrogant towards worshipping Allah; if they are arrogant, there is another group that worships Allah.
The second: that all of them are arrogant, and this is impossible as far as we know; but on the assumption that all created beings were arrogant towards worshipping Allah, Allah is free of need of them. All of this the Qur'an has stated clearly: ﴿Whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need of the worlds﴾; ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need of you﴾; ﴿If they disbelieve in it, then We have entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it﴾. That is when some disbelieve and some believe. ﴿So if they are arrogant, then those who are with your Lord﴾ [Fussilat 38]: that is when some are arrogant and some submit.
﴿So if they are arrogant, then those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day﴾: the clause ﴿fa-alladhina﴾ is the answer of the conditional and is joined with fa' because what follows it cannot be the verb of the condition; and this is a rule: when the answer of the conditional cannot correctly be the verb of the condition, it must be joined with fa', as Ibn Malik said:
"Join with fa' necessarily an answer, if it is made the condition for 'in' or others, it will not be made so."
Some who gathered what must be joined with fa' put it together in a verse:
"Nominal, demanding, and with a frozen (jāmid) form, and with mā, lan, qad, and with the future (tanfīs)."
﴿Those who are with your Lord﴾, namely the angels, ﴿glorify Him night and day﴾. The author says: (﴿glorify﴾ means: pray). This has a basis, since the context is about prostration; and we may say: they glorify by what is more general than prayer, that is, they say: "Subhan Allah" and "al-hamdu lillah," and what is similar to that, of everything that declares Allah, Mighty and Majestic, free of what is unbefitting to Him. His words ﴿yusabbihuna lahu﴾ mean: for Allah. Know that tasbih means declaring Him free (tanzih). So what is it that Allah is declared free of?
Allah, the Most High, is declared free of every deficiency. He, Mighty and Majestic, is free of every deficiency; no deficiency can afflict Him in any circumstance.
Second: He is declared free of every deficiency in His perfection; there is no deficiency in His hearing, His sight, His power or His strength.
Third: He is declared free of resemblance to created beings; a created being never resembles Him in any circumstance, and likeness between the Creator and the created is among the greatest impossibilities.

Therefore, what Allah is exalted above is three things. The first is deficiency: it is impossible for any deficiency to befall Him in any way whatsoever. The second is deficiency in His perfection: His perfect attributes, such as knowledge, power, life, hearing, sight, mercy and others, cannot be subject to any deficiency under any circumstances. The third is resemblance to the creation, which some call "mumathalah" (likeness) or "mushabahah" (similarity). Note this point: most of those who express this idea use the word mushabahah, and this is not correct. The correct approach is to express it in the words Allah used about Himself, when He said: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [ash-Shura 11], and He said: ﴿So do not set up for Allah comparisons﴾ [an-Nahl 74], and He never mentioned tashbih (resemblance) in any way whatsoever.

For this reason, expressing it with the negation of tamthil (likeness) is the correct formulation, rather than tashbih. The evidence that Allah is exalted above every deficiency and defect is His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest description﴾ [an-Nahl 60]. Al-mathal here means the description (wasf), because the word mathal is used in that sense, as in His saying: ﴿The description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered﴾ [Muhammad 15]. Here mathal means its description, its attributes: ﴿in it are rivers of water unaltered﴾, and so on. So if Allah has the highest description, that is, the most perfect, it necessarily follows that He is exalted above every deficiency.

As for deficiency in His perfection, His saying, blessed and exalted is He, proves it: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ [Qaf 38], meaning no deficiency. Despite the greatness of these creations, no deficiency befell Allah in them. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not fatigued by their creation, is able to give life to the dead?﴾ [al-Ahqaf 33].

The third: what is it? The resemblance of the created. Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [ash-Shura 11]. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So do not set up for Allah comparisons. Indeed, Allah knows and you do not know﴾ [an-Nahl 74]. He, exalted is He, also says: ﴿So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know﴾ [al-Baqarah 22]. Thus, tasbih means tanzih (exaltation above imperfection), and what Allah is exalted above is the three things you have now learned.

﴿They glorify Him by night and by day﴾: the particle "bi" here means "fi" (in), because the intended meaning is the time-frame of the night. Accordingly, "bi" carries the sense of "fi," as in His saying: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning, and by night; will you not then reason?﴾ [as-Saffat 137–138]: "bil-layl" means "fi al-layl," that is, "in the night."

His saying: ﴿by night and by day﴾ means that they glorify Allah at all times. He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿and they never tire﴾. Despite their glorifying Allah throughout the night and the day, ﴿they never tire﴾, meaning they do not become bored, and likewise they do not grow weary, because boredom arises from annoyance and fatigue and the humbling of the self in the face of what a person bears. These angels, peace be upon them, ﴿never tire﴾.

* There are benefits in the two verses. First: Allah has many signs that cannot be limited to two or three; we understand this from His saying: ﴿And among His signs﴾, and how numerous they are in the Noble Qur'an: ﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust﴾ [ar-Rum 20], ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves﴾ [ar-Rum 21], ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He has dispersed within them of creatures﴾ [ash-Shura 29], and they are many.

* A benefit of this noble verse: Allah, exalted is He, has perceptible signs that assist in understanding intellectual signs. This is from the mercy of Allah, mighty and majestic, that He showed His servants perceptible signs so that they could use them to understand intellectual signs. Everyone knows that every originated thing must have an originator. This is an intellectual sign that no one denies. For this reason He said: ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ [at-Tur 35]. The answer: neither this nor that. They were not created from nothing; rather, they must have a creator. Nor did they create themselves. Therefore they have a Creator, who is Allah, mighty and majestic.

For this reason, when Jubayr ibn Mut'im heard this verse, and he was among the captives of Badr, and he heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting Surat at-Tur and reach this verse, he said: "My heart nearly flew away"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3050) and Muslim (463/174), from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im.]]; meaning: I knew that I was mistaken, and that all the polytheists were mistaken. ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ The answer: neither this nor that. Thus it is necessary that they have a creator. Therefore the signs of Allah, mighty and majestic, are either intellectual or perceptible and heard. Here, among His signs are the night and the day. These signs are perceptible; everyone knows the night and the day, and that no one can bring them about.

* A benefit of this noble verse: the night, the day, the sun and the moon are great signs, and for this reason Allah mentioned them explicitly. The matter is as it is: this sun, the great, luminous, hot celestial body, no creature can ever make its like at all. We have explained the aspect of this during the course of the tafsir.

* A benefit of this noble verse: the prohibition of prostrating to the sun and the moon, based on His saying: ﴿Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon﴾, even though they are among the signs of Allah, but they are created, and prostration is due only to the Creator.

We move from this to an important point that Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, pointed out: that the attributes of Allah, mighty and majestic, are not Allah Himself. So it is not permissible to call upon an attribute, nor to prostrate to the attributes of Allah. For this reason Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Whoever calls upon an attribute of Allah is a disbeliever by consensus." That is, if someone said: "O Mercy of Allah, have mercy on me." How? Is mercy something separate from Allah, able to show mercy or not? No. So if you say: "O Mercy of Allah, have mercy on me," the meaning is that you have made another god alongside Allah, and this is disbelief.

Likewise, if you say: "O Power of Allah, rescue me," this is forbidden, it is shirk. Say instead: "O Allah, rescue me by Your power." It is not an objection to this that one says: "O Allah, by Your mercy I seek aid." Because the meaning is not that I am seeking aid from mercy as if I believed it to be an independent thing; rather the meaning is seeking a means to Allah, the Exalted, through His mercy, as if he were saying: "O Lord, aid me by Your mercy." So this matter must be carefully noted.

Among such errors also is the saying of some people: "The power of Allah willed it, the decree willed it." This is forbidden and not permissible. Power itself has no will; will belongs to Allah, mighty and majestic. As for power, it has no will, because it is an attribute in a described being, and the one who wills and chooses is Allah, mighty and majestic. But saying "the power of Allah necessitated such-and-such" is correct; that is, among the requirements of power are such-and-such. As for will, it exists only in one who possesses choice, and this cannot be the case for an attribute.

* A benefit of this noble verse: among the eloquence of the Qur'an is that when it mentions a ruling, it mentions the rational evidence for it. His saying: ﴿and prostrate to Allah, who created them﴾ ("prostrate to Allah") is a clear legal command, but ﴿who created them﴾ is a cosmic, decreed proof that the one deserving prostration is who? The One who created these things. How can you prostrate to the sun and the moon and not prostrate to Allah who created them? A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord who created you and those before you﴾ [al-Baqarah 21]. Another parallel is His saying: ﴿As for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right and said, "Who is stronger than us in strength?"﴾ Allah said: ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is stronger than them in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 15]. He did not say, "Did they not see that Allah is stronger than them?" Rather He said ﴿who created them﴾ to indicate, by clear rational proof, that they are less than Allah in power, because Allah is the One who created them. This is among the miraculous methods of the Qur'an that show it comes from One All-Wise, All-Aware.

* A benefit of this noble verse: a refutation of the worshippers of the sun and the moon, based on His saying: ﴿Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah﴾ [Fussilat 37]. Some scholars derived from this verse a benefit: the legislation of the eclipse prayer. They said: because Allah said: ﴿Among His signs are the night and the day, the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon﴾ and did not say "to the night and the day," this is because when the sun and the moon change, a worshipper of them may be moved to prostrate to them as one repenting. So He said: ﴿Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah who created them﴾. This deduction is somewhat remote, but it is not impossible that there is in this an indication of the legislation of the eclipse prayer.

* A benefit of this noble verse: it is impossible for a person who claims to truly worship Allah to prostrate to other than Allah, based on His saying: ﴿if you are indeed worshipping Him﴾.

* A benefit of this noble verse: a challenge to whoever associates others with Allah, in any kind of shirk, to be a true worshipper of Allah. For example, the one who shows off: we say, "You have not truly worshipped Allah; you did not single Him out in worship, because you intended by your worship to draw near to created beings." For this reason He said: ﴿if you are indeed worshipping Him﴾.

* A benefit of what follows this noble verse: those who are arrogant toward worshipping Allah will not harm Allah at all, based on His saying: ﴿But if they are arrogant, then those who are with your Lord﴾ [Fussilat 38].

* Among its benefits: the exposure of the challenge of those who worship other than Allah, that if they worship other than Allah, then Allah, mighty and majestic, has those who worship Him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: what some have used as evidence that the angels are better than humans, explaining it by the fact that there is no polytheist among the angels, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord do not refuse to worship Him﴾ [al-A'raf 206], whereas among the children of Adam there are believers and disbelievers. A kind that has no polytheist in it is better than a kind that contains both polytheists and monotheists. However, this argument may be objected to: the worship of a kind that contains both polytheist and monotheist is more excellent than the worship of a kind that has no polytheist, because of the hardship of monotheism within a kind that contains polytheists for the monotheist. So the monotheist among the children of Adam is better than the angels, because he worshipped Allah among a people who do not worship Allah, whereas the angels all worship Allah and do not refuse to worship Him. This question has differences among the scholars, and each has evidences. But Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, reconciled the evidences, saying: "The angels are better in terms of the beginning, and the righteous among humans are better in terms of the end." This is an acceptable view: reconciling the evidences that indicate preference, the preference of the angels over humans and of humans over the angels. For this reason al-Safarini, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"And in our view, the preference of the individual human beings
over the angels of our Lord is as is well known."

He said, meaning Imam Ahmad: "Whoever says other than this has fabricated." That is, whoever speaks without preferring the individuals of humankind over the angels is a fabricator. But the correct position is to say, as Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "As for the beginning, the angels are better, because they were created from light, do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded. But in the end, the righteous among humans have reward, recompense and nearness to Allah that the angels do not have."

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the angels have will. From where is this derived?

* Student: ﴿They glorify Him﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿They glorify Him﴾, and there is no glorification except by will.

From here we leap to the second benefit, which is: all created things, stones, trees, rivers, the sun, the moon, the heavens and the earth, have will, because they all glorify Allah: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing except that it glorifies His praise﴾ [al-Isra' 44]. By this we refute those who said that His saying ﴿wanting to collapse﴾ [al-Kahf 77], referring to the wall, is metaphorical, because the wall has no will. It is said: who told you it has no will? Rather it has will, and its inclination shows that it wanted. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said about Uhud: "It loves us and we love it,"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2889) and Muslim (1393/504), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] and love is more specific than will, and the Messenger, peace be upon him, affirmed it for the mountain.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: some scholars used it as evidence for the loftiness of Allah, and that created things are not all equal in nearness to Him, based on His saying: ﴿Those who are with your Lord﴾, and being "with" implies nearness, and that some created things are nearer to Allah than others. There is no difficulty in this. Who says that one who is in the lowest seventh earth is in nearness to Allah like one in the seventh heaven? No one says this. As for encompassing creation, there is no doubt that near and far are equal before Allah. But as for reality, there is no doubt that those in the heavens are nearer to Allah than those on earth. For this reason He said: ﴿Those who are with your Lord﴾.

I say that some scholars used this verse as evidence for the loftiness of Allah, and said: we are on earth, and those who are with Allah must be in heaven, because if He were not above, we too would be with Him. His saying ﴿Those who are with your Lord﴾, addressing those on earth, indicates the loftiness of Allah, mighty and majestic. This is undoubtedly a good deduction, but we do not need to bring this evidence, whose indication may be obscure to many people.

We have many clear proofs of the loftiness of Allah, mighty and majestic: rational proofs, traditional proofs, and innate proofs. No one denies the essential loftiness of Allah, mighty and majestic, except a deranged, unintelligent person, who is caught between two positions: either he says indwelling, or he says non-existence. Whoever denies the loftiness of Allah does not escape one of two things: either he says indwelling or non-existence. Indeed, they have committed to this. Those who denied Allah's loftiness divided into two groups. One group said: Allah is in every place, and did not exalt Allah above the latrines, the filth, the stench, and the markets where there is idle talk, lying and cheating. In my view, this is clear disbelief: whoever says that Allah in His essence is in every place is a disbeliever; if he dies, I will not pray over him or ask Allah's mercy for him, because he denies the Qur'an and the rational proofs, and attributes to his Lord every defect.

Others say: Allah, exalted is He, is neither inside the world, nor outside the world, nor connected to the world, nor separate, nor within, nor above, nor below, nor right, nor left. With what did they describe Allah? With non-existence. They described Allah with non-existence. If we were asked to describe the non-existent, we would not describe it with more than this. It is said: where is He? Since He is neither inside the world nor outside it, neither connected to it nor separate from it, neither above nor below nor right nor left, where does one go but to non-existence?

For this reason, when Ibn Furak said to Mahmud ibn Sebuktekin, may Allah have mercy on him: "I do not say that Allah is above the world, nor inside the world, nor below," and he mentioned these expressions, he said: "Explain to us the difference between the existence of your Lord and His non-existence," or words to that effect; meaning that if you describe Allah with these attributes, this is exactly non-existence.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 41, verse 37–38 (part 3 of 3):

In any case, affirming that Allah, exalted is He, is above, meaning His essential elevation (al-'uluw al-dhati), is a matter with no difficulty in it. What is strange is that you may come to an old woman who has not studied, has not understood, and has not learned, and ask her, "Where is Allah?" and she says, "In the sky." Unless the matter is as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: «His parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1359) and Muslim (2658/22) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]; that is, unless she is among a people who deny elevation, in which case she may deny it, on the basis that the environment changes. But if we approach the human being from the standpoint of his innate nature (fitrah), we would find him not doubting that Allah is in the sky.

For this reason al-Hamadhani (may Allah have mercy on him) silenced Abu al-Ma'ali al-Juwayni when Abu al-Ma'ali al-Juwayni was denying Allah's istiwa' (rising) over the Throne and saying: "Allah, exalted is He, was and there was no Throne, and He is now as He was." He wanted to deny His istiwa' over the Throne. Is the proof for Allah's istiwa' over the Throne rational or textual? Textual. That is, had Allah not informed us that He rose over the Throne, we would not have known it. Unlike elevation: the proof for elevation is rational, textual, and innate. Al-Hamadhani (may Allah have mercy on him) said to him: "O Shaykh, leave aside mention of the Throne. Tell us about this necessity. No knower has ever said, 'O Allah!' without finding in his heart a necessity to seek elevation." Ma qala 'arif qatt: "O Allah" ... The word ('arif) is a Sufi term; the 'arif in their usage is the one of broad knowledge, the one who worships much. No knower has ever said, "O Allah!" without finding in his heart a necessity to seek elevation. Is this correct or not?
* Student: Correct.
* Shaykh: Any person who says, "O Allah!" finds his heart turning toward the sky. So Abu al-Ma'ali cried out and began striking his head, saying: "Al-Hamadhani has bewildered me, has bewildered me," being unable to respond to this. So we say, praise be to Allah: elevation is a matter with no obscurity in it and no difficulty in it, and none denies it except a person immersed in innovation, may Allah protect us, and we regard him as a disbeliever, and that no prayer, charity, fasting or pilgrimage benefits him, and if he dies we do not pray over him.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the angels occupy all of time in worship, because of His saying: ﴿They glorify Him by night and day﴾. The "bi" (ba') here, although it may mean the adverbial sense of "in" (fi), which is the sense of time, still contains some indication of comprehensiveness, as Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿They glorify the night﴾. Look: ﴿They glorify the night and the day, and they do not slacken﴾ [al-Anbiya' 20].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of the strength of the angels, because of His saying: ﴿and they never tire﴾, meaning they do not grow bored or fatigued, which indicates their strength. The evidences for their strength are numerous, among them the story of Solomon (peace be upon him) when the hoopoe came to him with news of the queen of Sheba, that she had a great throne. Solomon said: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ [al-Naml 38]. Then ﴿a stronger one among the jinn said, "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place"﴾ [al-Naml 39], and he had a set time at which he would rise, ﴿and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾ [al-Naml 39], a jinn who wanted to bring it from the farthest part of Yemen to al-Sham, and he is one: he says ﴿I am strong for it﴾, emphasizing his strength, ﴿trustworthy﴾, I will not betray in it. ﴿One who had knowledge from the Scripture said, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you"﴾ [al-Naml 40]. Allahu akbar: immediately he found it before him. ﴿So when he saw it placed beside him, he said, "This is from the favor of my Lord"﴾ [al-Naml 40]. The fa' indicates sequence and immediacy. Then he said: ﴿when he saw it placed beside him﴾, and did not say, "when he saw it beside him, settled," as if it had been placed there for years. He said: ﴿This is from the favor of my Lord﴾. It had come from there in a moment; it is as if the throne were, for example, on your right and you moved it to your left, but even more swiftly. The people of knowledge said: this is because this one (the one with knowledge) invoked Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and so the angels carried it, and the angels are stronger than the jinn, and there is no doubt that they are stronger than the jinn.
﴿and they never tire﴾, then He said: ﴿And among His signs﴾ to the end.
* Student: The statement of Shaykh al-Islam that the angels are superior in the beginning and the humans are superior in the end (...).
* Shaykh: The angels are superior at the start, because they were created from light, they obey Allah's command, and among them there is none who is arrogant toward worshipping Allah. But in the end, the outcome of humans is better. Even the angels, on the Day of Resurrection, enter upon them from every gate, congratulating them, saying: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured﴾ [al-Ra'd 24], and they do not attain the bliss that the believers attain.
* Student: (...) the preference of righteous humans over the angels?
* Shaykh: No, not in a general sense.
* Student: No, in a specific sense for the righteous humans.
* Shaykh: (...) the righteous humans, that is not possible; even among the human species there are both disbelievers and believers.
* Student: In the matter of not worshipping Allah's attributes, you mentioned that it is impermissible. Also there is a common expression among the common people, namely their saying: "We thank Allah's favor," or a phrase similar to it that I do not recall now; that is, they thank Allah's favor, may He be exalted.
* Shaykh: Mention it now so we know.
* Student: "We praise Allah and thank His favor."
* Shaykh: Yes. Does not Allah, blessed and exalted, say: ﴿And be thankful for the favor of Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 114]?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: And what is meant is the created favor of Allah, not the attribute; that is, what Allah has bestowed. Likewise, "I thank Allah's favor" does not mean that I make this attribute the object of thanks, but rather that this favor which Allah has bestowed upon me, I thank Allah for it.
* Student: So this expression is permissible?
* Shaykh: There is nothing wrong with it.
* Student: Our saying, O Shaykh, ﴿bi al-layli wa al-nahar﴾: that the "ba'" here means "fi." The scholars of Basra, who deny that letters may take the place of one another, do not hold the doctrine of taḍmīn (implicit meaning). How do you answer such verses?
* Shaykh: We, may Allah bless you, have a rule: if the Qur'an indicates something permissible, then the opinion of one who opposes it is not considered. That is first.
Second: if the grammarians differ on a question, and there is no legal evidence supporting one side or the other, we follow the easier view. I have given our students this rule: if you see the scholars of Basra and the scholars of Kufa differing on something, follow the easier one and say, "Praise be to Allah for the ease." Take this rule with you, God willing, to carry it to your people.
* Student: (...) because Shaykh al-Islam makes errors...
* Shaykh: No, he does not err in such matters. Shaykh al-Islam is strict when the verb is construed with a meaning that suits the preposition, such as: ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah drink﴾ [al-Insan 6]. Some say: "bihā" means that the ba' means "min," "they drink from it." We say: no; it is better to construe the verb with a meaning that fits the particle. As for the verses before us, ﴿they glorify Him by night﴾, that does not hold up.
* Student: May Allah be good to you. Those who say: Allah is neither within the world nor outside it, nor such-and-such (...), do we not pray over them?
* Shaykh: No, by Allah, I cannot rule them to be disbelievers.
* Student: The rational proofs, O Shaykh, for Allah's elevation (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, that does not contradict it, but they say: we do not deny Allah's elevation, but we interpret it as elevation of meaning, that He is elevated in power, elevated in hearing, elevated in sight, and similar things.
* Student: (...) you say magic is a knowledge, and they cite this verse: ﴿one who had knowledge from the Scripture﴾. How do we respond to these people?
* Shaykh: Magic? We say magic is a knowledge. Did not Allah say of the two angels: ﴿and they teach no one until they say, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." And they learn from them that by which they separate a man from his wife﴾ [al-Baqarah 102]? There is no problem in its being knowledge.
* Student: They cite this verse.
* Shaykh: No, that is not correct. As if they want to say that this one is a magician?! The one who had knowledge from the Scripture said: ﴿knowledge from the Scripture﴾ [al-Naml 40]; he did not say knowledge of magic. Moreover, magic cannot change realities. Magic makes things appear otherwise, meaning it makes the one under its effect see the still as moving and the moving as still. As for its being (...).

**Student:** ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth lifeless. But when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who revived it is the One who will surely revive the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent.﴾ (41:39) ﴿Indeed, those who distort Our verses are not hidden from Us. So is he who is thrown into the Fire better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do as you wish; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ (41:40) ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them [will be held accountable]. And indeed, it is a mighty Book. Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.﴾ (41:41-42)

* **The Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth lifeless﴾. The particle ﴿min﴾ ("among") is for partitive meaning (li-l-tab'id). ﴿Ayat﴾ is the plural of ﴿ayah﴾, which is a specific sign that identifies what it indicates. Every sign that specifies and determines its referent is an ayah.

﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth lifeless﴾. The address ﴿annaka﴾ ("that you") here is directed to everyone who is capable of being addressed, and is not specific to the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family. Know that an address directed to a single person is of three kinds:

The first: what evidence shows is specific to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which is then specific to him. The second: what evidence shows is general, which is then general. The third: what has no evidence either way, so it may be specific to the Messenger or directed to everyone who can be addressed. In the Exalted's saying ﴿Did We not expand your breast for you? And We removed from you your burden﴾ (94:1-2), the address is specific to the Messenger, peace be upon him, since this cannot apply to anyone else. In His saying ﴿O Messenger, deliver what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ (5:67), this too is specific to him. In His saying ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period﴾ (65:1), this is general, as evidenced by the fact that He says ﴿O Prophet﴾ and then ﴿when you divorce﴾. Most addresses have no evidence either way, so we say: either it is directed to the Messenger, peace be upon him, and his community follows him in that, or it is said to be an address to everyone who can be addressed. In this verse, ﴿that you see the earth﴾: is the address here specific to the Messenger? No, rather it is general to him and to others, either because others are included in the original address, or by implication.

(﴿That you see the earth lifeless﴾, i.e., dry and barren, with no plants at all. ﴿When We send down upon it water﴾, meaning rain. ﴿It stirs﴾, i.e., moves. ﴿And swells﴾, i.e., becomes puffed up and rises.) ﴿When We send down upon it water﴾, i.e., rainwater. ﴿It stirs﴾, i.e., its vegetation stirs upon it, and the intended meaning is not that the earth itself moves, since we do not perceive that. Although we permit that its movement may be a slight movement, what appears is that it stirs with plants. ﴿And swells﴾, i.e., rises up.

Is the intended meaning what the author indicated, the swelling of the earth when the seed wants to emerge? The seed swells beneath the earth, and then when its shoot wants to come out, it raises the earth. Is this the meaning of (swells)? Or the meaning is: it rises with vegetation? Both are possible: it rises with plants, and since He mentioned its stirring first, the light stirring of plants, He then mentioned the rising of plants, the large trees that tower. All of this is possible.

Then He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, He who revived it is the One who will surely revive the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent﴾. ﴿Indeed, He who revived it﴾, i.e., who revived the lifeless earth, ﴿is the One who will surely revive the dead﴾. As you see, the sentence is emphasized by two emphatics: ﴿inna﴾ and the ﴿lam﴾. ﴿Al-mawta﴾ is the plural of ﴿mayyit﴾, and the intended meaning is everyone who has died among the children of Adam and others. He is capable of reviving them.

﴿Indeed, He is over all things competent﴾. ﴿Innahu﴾ is also an emphasized sentence with ﴿inna﴾, and ﴿over all things competent﴾: Allah is competent over everything. He is capable of bringing into existence what does not exist, capable of annihilating what exists, capable of changing what is fixed and of fixing what changes. He is capable of everything.

* In this verse there are benefits. First: among Allah's signs that indicate His power is that the dry, lifeless earth, when water descends upon it, sprouts, stirs, and swells. Can anyone do such a thing? Never. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Have you considered what you plow? Is it you who grow it, or are We the growers?﴾ (56:63-64). No one, however strong, can produce a single leaf. Allah, the Exalted, has challenged all creation, saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke other than Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ (22:73). This is a challenge concerning the cosmic, decreed matter. And Allah challenged creation concerning the legislative matter, saying: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce its like﴾ (17:88). Thus man is helpless, however great he is.

* Among the benefits of this verse: inferring the unseen promised from the observed perceptible. Its aspect is that Allah argued from something seen and perceptible, which is the earth's vegetation after it had been lifeless, to something awaited, which is the reviving of the dead after their death.

* Also in it: reasoning by rational evidence, that a person infers the rational from the perceptible. That is, Allah's power over this indicates His power over the Hereafter.

* Among its benefits also: the use of analogy (qiyas), and that analogy is valid, since Allah, the Exalted, analogized the reviving of the dead to the reviving of the earth.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: emphasizing what should be emphasized, whether to reject a denial, to address someone's doubt, or to stress the importance of the matter. Emphases are either for the importance of the matter, or to remove doubt and hesitation about something so that it becomes a certain matter, or to establish a denied thing. For example, if the verse addresses those who deny resurrection, this emphasis is to establish something denied, meaning to establish a thing that a people rejected. If the verse addresses those who hesitate about it, the emphasis removes doubt and hesitation. If we assume it addresses someone who has no doubt or denial, then it is for the importance of the matter and the importance of the subject, because belief in it is what drives a person to act. Were a person not to believe that he will be resurrected and recompensed, he would not be energetic in action. What most energizes a person to act is his fear of the Day of Resurrection.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the generality of Allah's power, the Exalted, from His saying ﴿Indeed, He is over all things competent﴾. Nothing can overcome Him, due to the completeness of His knowledge and the completeness of His power. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And Allah was not to be caused to fail by anything in the heavens or on the earth. Indeed, He is ever Knowing and Competent﴾ (35:44). Inability arises either from lack of knowledge or from lack of power; Allah, the Exalted, negated inability and showed that this is due to the perfection of His knowledge and power. So: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ (2:20).

Al-Jalal al-Suyuti (may Allah forgive us and him) mentioned, in Surat al-Ma'idah, an objectionable statement. He said: "He specified the intellect (of Himself), so He is not competent over Himself." It is as though he is saying: He is competent over everything except Himself; He is not competent over Himself. This is without doubt an objectionable statement. It is as though he is saying, for example: Is Allah, the Exalted, capable of annihilating Himself? In his words, we say: this is a baseless statement, because power relates only to a possible thing. As for an impossible thing, it is impossible. It is not impossible for our power; no, what is impossible for our power is not impossible for Allah's power. But what is impossible in its own essence cannot be the object of any power or anything other than power, except knowledge. For this reason al-Safarini said in his creed:

*By a power that relates to the possible* ∗∗∗ .......................

So it is said to al-Jalal, may Allah pardon us and him: if you mean that Allah is not capable of annihilating Himself, this is not a matter that arises at all, because power does not relate to this. If you mean that He is not capable of descending to the lowest heaven, coming to judge between His servants, establishing Himself upon His Throne, and similar voluntary acts, this is false. Rather, He is capable of all that. But al-Suyuti (may Allah pardon us and him) is among those who hold that voluntary acts do not subsist in Allah. That is, he says: Allah cannot descend, establish Himself, or come on the Day of Resurrection, because in his view these are occurrences, and occurrences relate only to occurrences.

In any case, this is a philosophy brought by the people of kalam (scholastic theology), and how much they have brought of speech. Their speech is speech upon speech, with no benefit in it: prolixity without benefit, wasting of time without benefit, leading to doubt and hesitation without benefit. For this reason some said: the people most prone to doubt at death are the people of kalam. We seek refuge in Allah. Why? Because they did not build their creed upon the Book and the Sunnah; they built it upon illusions they took to be rational, so they went astray and led others astray.

We say as our Lord, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ (2:20), only, and that is sufficient. As for knowledge, it is broader than power, because knowledge relates to the necessary, the impossible, and the possible. That is, Allah's knowledge relates to everything, even to the impossible. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Had there been within them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ (21:22). This is impossible, yet knowledge relates to it. And ﴿If the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted﴾ (23:71). This too is impossible according to the wisdom of Allah, the Exalted.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: inferring the specific from the general. Allah argued for His power to revive the dead with two proofs: one specific and one general. What is the specific? The reviving of the earth after its death. The general: ﴿Indeed, He is over all things competent﴾ (41:39). From this benefit it follows that a general statement encompasses all its individual instances. The Prophet ﷺ mentioned this in his saying when he taught his community the tashahhud: "When you do that, you have greeted every righteous servant in the heavens and on the earth."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1202) and Muslim (402/55), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]] For example, if a man says: "My houses are endowed (waqf)," does that include all his houses? 

* **Student:** Yes.

* **The Shaykh:** And if he says: "My cars belong to so-and-so," that includes all the cars. If he says: "My wives are divorced," that includes every wife he has. If he says: "My slaves are free," that includes every slave. The point is that a general term encompasses all its individual instances.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 41, verse 40 (part 1 of 4):

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our verses are not hidden from Us﴾ [Fussilat 40]. The mufassir says: (Those who deviate, and deviate [from it]). From (alhada) comes yulhidun, and from (lahada) comes yalhadun. The origin of al-lahd (the root) or al-ilhad is al-mayl (inclination), and from it the grave-niche is called lahd because it inclines to the side of the grave. So from where does this root (l-h-d) derive? From inclination. The meaning of ﴿yulhiduna fi ayatina﴾ is: they incline concerning them. And ﴿ayatina﴾ is the plural of ayah, and the signs of Allah, may He be exalted, are divided into two kinds:

Legislative signs (ayat shar'iyyah): the revelation sent down to the prophets and messengers. And cosmic signs (ayat qadariyyah): the created things. All created things are cosmic signs pointing to their Creator and Originator. On this the truthful poet says:

How strange that the Deity is disobeyed, or how the denier can deny Him,
And in everything there is for Him a sign that shows that He is One.

Every created thing is a sign of Allah. So the signs are of two kinds: cosmic (kawniyyah), which is all created things, and legislative (shar'iyyah), which is the revelation sent down to the messengers, upon them be prayers and peace.

Deviation concerning the cosmic signs occurs in one of three matters: either by attributing them to other than Allah, or by believing that someone shares with Allah in them, or by believing that someone assists Allah in them. How many is that? Three. The first: attributing them to other than Allah, as when one says, for example: "The one who created the heavens is the natural force." This is deviation concerning the cosmic signs. Or believing that someone shares with Allah in them, such as saying: "The one who governs the universe is Allah and the such-and-such Imam," as some of the Rafidah say. The third: believing that someone assists Allah in them, meaning as if Allah were unable to establish the heavens and the earth so another helped Him. This is deviation concerning the cosmic signs of Allah.

To this the saying of the Most High points: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and they have no partnership in either, and He has no supporter among them﴾ [Saba 22]. All three are negated: ﴿they do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth﴾ by way of independent ownership; ﴿and they have no partnership in either﴾ by way of sharing; ﴿and He has no supporter among them﴾, that is, for Allah, ﴿no supporter﴾, meaning no helper.

Once more we say: what is deviation concerning the cosmic signs?
* A student: It occurs in three things: either by attributing them to other than Allah, or believing that someone shares with Allah, or believing that someone assists Allah.
* The Shaykh: Either by attributing them to other than Allah, or believing that someone shares with Allah in them, or believing that someone assists Allah in them. All of this is deviation.

We said that the legislative signs are what was revealed to the messengers of Allah. Deviation concerning them occurs by denying them, distorting them, or opposing them, also in three matters: denial, distortion, or opposition. This is deviation concerning the legislative signs. So whoever denies them and says that Muhammad, for example, received no revelation but is taught by a human, he is a deviator. Whoever distorts them and changes their meaning or their wording, he is a deviator, because distortion can be in wording and can be in meaning. The third: whoever opposes them is a deviator. Whoever disobeys Allah is a deviator, but it is not the deviation we understand, which is leaving the religion; rather he is a deviator to the extent of the sin and opposition he commits. The evidence for that is the saying of the Most High: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing, We will make him taste a painful punishment﴾ [al-Hajj 25]. This evidence is textual. The rational evidence is that we said deviation in language is inclination, and the disobedient one who opposes the commands is clearly inclined. Deviation concerning the legislative signs occurs by how many?

* A student: By three.
* The Shaykh: By three, or by one of three?
* A student: By one of three; either by denying them, distorting them, or opposing them.
* The Shaykh: Correct. Those who deviate in this or in that, the Most High says: ﴿are not hidden from Us﴾ [Fussilat 40]. This is a negative expression, ﴿are not hidden﴾. Allah, may He be exalted, negated that these would be hidden from Him. Why? Because of the perfection of His knowledge. Know that it is impossible to find in the attributes of Allah a pure negation; rather, everything Allah negates of Himself includes a perfection and an affirmation. Hold onto this as a principle and do not neglect it: there is no pure negation in the attributes of Allah; rather, everything Allah negates of Himself includes a perfection. So for example: ﴿are not hidden from Us﴾, why? Because of the perfection of Our knowledge, for Allah, the Exalted, has perfect knowledge encompassing everything. ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private conversation? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ [az-Zukhruf 80].

So ﴿are not hidden from Us﴾ means: their state and their persons are not hidden from Us, because of the perfection of Our knowledge. The purpose of this sentence is a warning, as you say to your son: "O my son, go wherever you wish, for you are not hidden from me; your deed is not hidden from me." Its purpose is a warning, and it is in the extreme of warning, because when Allah, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our verses are not hidden from Us﴾, the sinews will tremble from this threat.

Then he said: (﴿are not hidden from Us﴾, so We will recompense them). The author, may Allah have mercy on him, says: (﴿concerning Our verses﴾, the Qur'an, by denial). There is deficiency in the mufassir's explanation. First: he made the verses here the legislative signs, and this is an error; the signs are more general. Second: he did not make deviation in the legislative signs except one type, which is denial, whereas we have said that deviation concerning them occurs in one of three matters: either denial, distortion, or opposition.

Allah the Most High said: ﴿Is he who is thrown into the Fire better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ [Fussilat 40]. The answer: the second or the first?

* A student: The second: ﴿he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Is he who is thrown into the Fire﴾ is a question from Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Is he who is thrown into the Fire better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ The answer is undoubtedly the second. The phrase ﴿Is he who is thrown﴾ is a result of His saying ﴿are not hidden from Us﴾. So the meaning is: they are not hidden from Us, and We will throw them into the Fire, because this is the result of His saying ﴿are not hidden from Us﴾. So the meaning is: they are not hidden from Us, and We will throw them into the Fire. Tell me: ﴿Is he who is thrown into the Fire better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ The answer is that people will say with one voice: he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection is the better.

As for His saying ﴿he who is thrown into the Fire is better﴾, the word ﴿yulqa﴾ indicates that the people of the Fire, may Allah protect us, when they reach it, do not enter it willingly or by choice; rather they are thrown with force, as a stone is thrown from a mountain. The Most High said: ﴿Every time a company is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them﴾ [al-Mulk 8]: ﴿every time it is thrown into it﴾. And the Most High said: ﴿On the Day they will be pushed toward the Fire of Hell with a violent push﴾ [at-Tur 13], because they do not wish to go. But it has been established that the Fire will appear to them like a mirage, so they come to it hastily. We say: there is no contradiction; it appears to them like a mirage, and they want to drink, so they come to it hastily. When they reach it and recognize that it is the Fire, they stop, and then they are pushed into the Fire of Hell with a violent push, may Allah protect us and you from it, and then they are thrown into it with force.

As for His saying ﴿better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection﴾, they are the believers who do not deviate concerning the signs of Allah. These come on the Day of Resurrection secure. The Most High said: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with wrongdoing, those will have security﴾ [al-An'am 82]. In this world or in the Hereafter?

* Students: In this world and the Hereafter.
* The Shaykh: In this world and the Hereafter. ﴿Or who comes secure﴾: why is ﴿secure﴾ in the accusative when it is preceded by a present-tense verb?
* A student: As a circumstantial accusative (hal).
* The Shaykh: A circumstantial accusative. Where is the subject?
* A student: The subject is the pronoun in ﴿yaati﴾.
* The Shaykh: The subject is an implied pronoun; the reckoning is: or who comes, he being secure on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿The Day of Resurrection﴾ refers to the Day of Resurrection and Rising. It is called the Day of Resurrection for three reasons. The first: people stand in it from their graves before the Lord of the Worlds, as the Most High said: ﴿The day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 6]. The second: justice is established in it, as the Most High said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Anbiya' 47]. The third: witnesses stand in it: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believed in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 51]. So it is called the Day of Resurrection for three reasons. Brother?

* A student: Either because people rise from their graves.
* The Shaykh: Because people rise from their graves before the Lord of the Worlds. The evidence?
* A student: ﴿The day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds﴾.
* The Shaykh: That is one. The second?
* A student: The second: the standing of the witnesses.
* The Shaykh: Yes. The evidence?
* A student: ﴿And the day the witnesses stand﴾.
* The Shaykh: The third?
* A student: The third: the standing of the scales with justice.
* The Shaykh: That justice is established in it. The evidence?
* A student: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection﴾.
* The Shaykh: May Allah bless you. ﴿Or who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection. Do whatever you wish﴾: meaning, after this warning, threat and menace, ﴿Do whatever you wish﴾. This phrase too undoubtedly conveys a threat: do whatever you wish of good or evil. ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾ [Fussilat 40]. Therefore ﴿Do whatever you wish﴾ is not a permission that a person may do whatever he wills, as those disbelievers claim that freedom means doing whatever you want. For those disbelievers, a person is free in his religion, he adheres to whatever he wishes; free in his morals, he adopts whatever manners he wishes; free in his deeds, he does whatever he wishes; this is how they see it. We say: no. Absolute freedom is absolute slavery, because when you free yourself from the bonds of the Sharia, you become bound by the bonds of evil. For this reason Ibn al-Qayyim says in his Nuniyyah:

They fled from the slavery for which they were created,
...........................

What is the slavery for which we were created? The worship of Allah, the Exalted. ﴿Wa-bulu﴾, meaning: they were tried, with the slavery of the self and the devil: they became slaves to their souls and to the devils. They fled from their slavery to Allah into their slavery to desire and Satan. So we say: His saying ﴿Do whatever you wish﴾ is not an unrestricted permission, not a license; rather it is a threat, and it is a clear Arabic style since the Qur'an was revealed until today. For this reason He reinforced it with His saying ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾. The author said: (a threat to them). The pronoun ﴿innahu﴾ refers to Allah, the Exalted. His saying ﴿Seeing of what you do﴾ means: All-Knowing. The phrase ﴿Seeing of what you do﴾ is placed before its governing verb for two reasons:

One is verbal, the other is semantic. As for the verbal reason, it is to match the verse-endings (ru'us al-ayat) with one another. The Qur'an, as you know, was revealed in Arabic language that observes both verbal and semantic harmony. The second benefit: it is more threatening than if it came after its governing element. It is as if He says: if He were not knowing of anything, He would still be knowing of your deeds. Here the restriction serves to show the threat to them, as if He says: if everything were hidden from Him, your deeds would not be hidden from Him.

* Benefits of this verse:
* First: the prohibition of deviation concerning the signs of Allah. The reason is that Allah threatened those who deviate concerning His signs.
* Second: the affirmation of the signs, and the division is from our own inductive investigation. The verse does not state this explicitly; rather, through investigation and induction we know that the signs of Allah are divided into two kinds: legislative and cosmic.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the threat to the deviators that Allah is aware of them, and nothing of their states is hidden from Him.
* Among its benefits: the vastness of the knowledge of Allah, blessed and exalted, and that nothing is hidden from Him.
* Among its benefits: that deviation is a cause of entering the Fire, by His saying ﴿Is he who is thrown into the Fire﴾, like the deviators.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the people of the Fire, may Allah protect us, are thrown into it with force and pushed toward it with a violent push, as humiliation and disgrace for them, by His saying ﴿Is he who is thrown into the Fire﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of comparing two things whose difference is greater than that between the heaven and the earth, to silence the opponent. The evidence: ﴿Is he who is thrown into the Fire better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection﴾. Everyone knows the second is better, and there is no need for the question, but it is for silencing the opponent and establishing the proof against him. A parallel is His saying: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ [an-Naml 59]. Everyone knows Allah is better, but this is for silencing the opponent. And from it His saying: ﴿Say: Are you more knowing, or is Allah?﴾ [al-Baqarah 140]. Everyone knows the more knowing is Allah, but this too is for silencing the opponent. This is a benefit, so pay attention: in comparing two things whose disparity is evident, the purpose is not to make a comparison but to silence the opponent.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever remains upright concerning the signs of Allah and does not deviate concerning them will come on the Day of Resurrection secure, by His saying ﴿or who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection﴾ in contrast to the deviators who are thrown into the Fire.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the greatness of Allah, the Exalted, and the strength of His authority, by His saying ﴿Do whatever you wish﴾, for such a threat comes only from one of perfect authority.
* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of the Day of Resurrection, by His saying ﴿the Day of Resurrection﴾.
* Also: that people on the Day of Resurrection are between secure and fearful, by His saying ﴿or who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the servant's will, by His saying ﴿Do whatever you wish﴾. In this is a refutation of the Jabriyyah. The Jabriyyah say that a human is compelled in his actions and has no will in what he does. How strange they are: he prays without will, performs ablution without will, walks without will, sits without will, believes without will, disbelieves without will. Glory be to Allah! Compelled?! They say: yes, compelled. This movement is natural in him, like burning in fire. Does fire burn by its own choice? No, but burning is placed in it. They say: these actions and movements of a human are involuntary, but he was made to have them. They say: his voluntary movement is like his involuntary movement. A man descending the stairs from top to bottom and climbing from bottom to top is like one who is rolled down a staircase. Is the one rolled down a staircase one who has choice, or one who has no choice?

* A student: He has no choice.
* The Shaykh: They say: whoever descends by his own choice is the same. It was said to them: if that is so, then among the greatest injustices is that Allah punishes the wrongdoer, because the wrongdoer says: I am compelled, I have no power and no choice. They said: impossible. Is injustice toward Allah impossible in its essence? No, because He does not will it, but it is impossible in its essence. Why? Because they would say: the Creator's disposal of His dominion is not injustice, and whoever disposes of his own dominion is not unjust. For this reason Ibn al-Qayyim said of them:

And injustice, to them, is impossible in its very essence,
..........................

We say: you are mistaken. Allah, exalted is He, has legislated laws, threatened those who oppose them, and promised those who comply with them. He has given man freedom. Injustice is possible with regard to Allah, but it is impossible for Him by His will, meaning that He does not will injustice. Had He willed, He could have acted unjustly, but He does not will it, and it is absolutely not an attribute of His. Allah says: ﴿And your Lord is never unjust to the servants﴾, and He says: ﴿The word does not change with Me, and I am not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Qaf 29]. And He says, negating the will of injustice: ﴿And Allah does not intend injustice for the servants﴾ [Ghafir 31]. How could Allah, Mighty and Majestic, be praised for something impossible? That is not possible. Were injustice not possible, it would not have been described as a perfection of Allah. Is it possible for Him to punish a person who spent his night and day in obedience to Allah? Is that possible rationally or not? It is rationally possible, but Allah, exalted is He, does not will this. Therefore, their claim that injustice is impossible with respect to the Creator, because He disposes of His own dominion, is refuted.

In any case, in this verse, ﴿Do as you wish﴾ is evidence for establishing will for the servant, and it clearly refutes the Jabriyya (determinists). It is strange that some people arose against the Jabriyya and countered innovation with innovation. They said: man has will, volition and choice, but it is separate from the will and volition of Allah, exalted is He; he acts independently, with no will of Allah in it at all. How? He says: Yes, you now go and come by your own choice; you do not feel that anyone is forcing or compelling you, so Allah has no connection with your action. You act by choice, independent of the will of the Creator.

Which of the two is closer to reason, the Jabriyya or the Qadariyya (free-will advocates)? The Qadariyya is closer to reason, because every person knows that he does a thing by his own choice, and that he is praised for doing good and blamed for doing evil. Had it been without choice, he would not deserve praise for good or blame for evil. Everyone knows this, and that is why they are called the Rationalists, because they apply reason even to matters like this. So we say: the innovation of the Jabriyya was countered with the innovation of whom?
* Students: The Qadariyya.
* The Shaykh: The Qadariyya who affirmed for man an independent will. For this reason they are called the Magians of this Ummah, because the Magians (majus) say: events have two creators, Darkness and Light. Whatever evil there is in the world, its creator is Darkness; whatever good is in it, its creator is Light. Since all things in the world are either good or evil, there must be two gods: a god of good and a god of evil. Which is more suited to good? Light, because light has expansiveness of the chest and openness. Which is more suited to evil? Darkness. They said: therefore everything that happens in the universe has two creators: darkness and light. Darkness creates evil, and light creates good. On this, al-Mutanabbi says in praise of his patron:

How many a gift of the darkness of night is with you
Tells that the Manichaeans are lying.

("Kam" is for multiplicity.) "How many a gift of the darkness of night is with you," meaning: how many a blessing. "Tells that the Manichaeans": they are a sect of the Magians. "Are lying," because the Manichaeans say: darkness creates what?
* Students: Evil.
* The Shaykh: And blessings, are they good or evil? Good. He tells his patron: you are generous night and day, which refutes the Manichaeans who say that darkness creates evil. In any case, we say: the Jabriyya's innovation was countered with an innovation. Know that innovation cannot be countered with innovation, because...

........................
Tells that the Manichaeans are lying.
("Kam" is for multiplicity.)
How many a gift of the darkness of night is with you,
.................................
Meaning: of blessing. "Tells that the Manichaeans" are a sect of the Magians. "Are lying," because the Manichaeans say: darkness creates what?
* Student: Evil.
* The Shaykh: And blessings, are they good or evil?
* Student: Good.
* The Shaykh: Good. He tells his patron: you are generous night and day, which refutes the Manichaeans who say that darkness creates evil. In any case, we say: the Jabriyya's innovation was countered with what? With an innovation. Know that innovation cannot be countered with innovation, because when you innovate, he will bring a claim against you, and you against him. Among this is what some people do on the day of 'Ashura. On 'Ashura, for the Rafidah (Shi'a), it is a day of sorrow and calamity. Some people from Ahl al-Sunnah came and said: then let us make it a day of joy and happiness. On 'Ashura we should adorn ourselves, beautify ourselves, be generous to our dependents, cheer them up and show them things, the opposite of what? The opposite of sorrow. But is this correct? No, because if we do this, the Rafidah will say: what is your evidence for this? So innovation can never be countered with innovation; it is countered only with the Sunnah. We counter the Jabriyya, who deny the servant's will, with the evidence of the Book and the Sunnah that man has a will. And we counter the Qadariyya by (the verse) that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and ﴿you do not will except that Allah wills﴾. Do you understand? So when I will something and do it, I say: Allah willed that before I willed it. It is impossible for me to will something and do it without Allah, exalted is He, having willed it, ever. If someone says: if you say this, and that your will comes after the will of Allah and follows it, then it follows that the disobedient person would argue against us with the decree and will of Allah. The disobedient person wills disobedience and does disobedience. We say to him: why? He says: because Allah willed that. You say that there is no will of the servant except that it is preceded by the will of Allah, ﴿and you do not will except that Allah wills﴾ [al-Insan 30]. What should I do? Allah willed that I do it, so I did it. How can you blame me for a matter that Allah decreed upon me and willed for me? What do we say? We say: first of all, who told you that Allah willed that? Does anyone know that Allah willed a thing except after its occurrence? No one knows. ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾ [Luqman 34]. For example, when I stand and pray, I know that when I willed the prayer and did it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had willed it beforehand. But before I pray, do I know that Allah willed that I pray or not?
* Students: We do not know.
* The Shaykh: No? Are you sure?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Fine. When the disobedient person commits disobedience, does he know that Allah willed for him to commit disobedience before he committed it? No. Then he has no argument. How well did some scholars say: the decree is a hidden secret, not known until the decreed matter occurs. And that is so. This is a decisive answer that the criminal cannot get past by a hair's breadth. Then we say to him: now, if there was a blazing fire in front of you or drowning valleys, would you not refrain from them and not advance toward them?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Fine. Why then do you not advance and throw yourself into the fire, saying: by Allah, this is the will of Allah? It is impossible for someone to advance either toward drowning valleys or toward a blazing fire and claim that this is by the will of Allah; that is impossible. We say: then why did you not avoid the acts of disobedience which you knew, through the promise or threat of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are a cause for entering the Fire? Why? We address this to him when we want him to avoid acts of disobedience. When we want him to perform acts of obedience, we say: come. A competition was announced in the newspapers for two positions: one pays ten thousand riyals a month, and the other twelve riyals a month. Where does he go?
* Students: Ten thousand.
* The Shaykh: No, folks, he goes to the ten, and we say this is the decree of Allah?
* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: No? Are you sure?
* Students: Yes.

Shaykh: Alright, let us say: Do you not go to the ten thousand? You want this good salary. Likewise, righteous deeds are presented to you: that the reward of a good deed is ten times its like, up to seven hundred times. Why do you not undertake them? Just as you pursue what you see as good fortune in worldly work, why do you not pursue what you see as good fortune in the work of the Hereafter? And by this the argument of the wrongdoer is cut off, whether he wrongs himself by committing the forbidden acts or by abandoning the obligatory duties, there is no harm (...). We say that we have touched on this, although it is not among the specialities of the science of tafsir, because this is an important matter of 'aqidah (creed). Such objections from the Jabriyyah or the Qadariyyah may confuse a person, so we say what you have heard. The matter, praise be to Allah, is clear. Indeed, the Messenger ﷺ resolved this problem in just two words. He said, ﷺ, while standing at the edge of the grave of one of his daughters: "There is none of you but that his place has been written, of Paradise or of the Fire" (there is none but that his place has been written, of Paradise and of the Fire). They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not leave off action and rely upon what has been written?" This is an objection, but it is an objection at first glance, as Allah the Most High said: ﴿Baadiya ar-ra'y﴾ [Hud 27]. As long as what is written is written, what need is there to act? If this one is written among the people of happiness, then he has attained happiness, so let him sleep, because he is among the people of happiness. And this one, from the people of wretchedness, likewise does not act, because he is among the people of wretchedness, so what need is there for him to act? The Prophet ﷺ then said two words: "Act, for each is made easy for that for which he was created."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4945) and Muslim (2647 / 7) from the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.]] Subhan Allah, he did not go on with philosophy and lengthy discussion; in two words: "Act, for each is made easy for that for which he was created." This is what is on our side: that we act, and then each is made easy for that for which he was created. So if you find within yourself that Allah has made good, guidance and energy for worship easy for you, then know that you are among those written among the people of happiness, due to the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "As for the people of happiness, they are made easy for the work of happiness, and as for the people of wretchedness, they are made easy for the work of the people of wretchedness."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1362) and Muslim (2647 / 6) from the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.]] So the matter, praise be to Allah, is very clear: there is no argument for the sinner by the decree, for what? For his disobedience. Nor for the one who is negligent by the decree, for his negligence. The matter is too clear to need much discussion. But since Satan comes to a person and says such-and-such, it remains for us to say: Did not Adam argue by the decree? Did not Allah the Most High argue by the decree when He said to His Messenger: ﴿Had Allah willed, they would not have associated⁠﴾ [al-An'am 107]? So what is the answer? The answer is to say: As for the words of Allah the Most High: ﴿Had Allah willed, they would not have associated, nor have We made you a guardian over them﴾ [al-An'am 107], this is consolation for the Messenger ﷺ, a consolation to him, for Allah said to him: ﴿Had Allah willed, they would not have associated⁠﴾. Their association is by the will of Allah. And it is known that the Messenger ﷺ would be content with what? With the decree of Allah. He would be content with the decree of Allah. Therefore we must look at the people of sin with two views, or two perspectives: the decreed perspective and the legislated perspective. The decreed perspective is that we accept what has occurred of their disobedience, because it is by whose decree? By the decree of Allah. The legislated perspective is that we bind them to the law of Allah, we establish upon them the prescribed punishments (hudud), discretionary punishments (ta'zir) and other things that move them to perform acts of obedience and abandon what is forbidden. Pay attention, my brothers, these issues are very important. So we say: the words of Allah to the Messenger: ﴿Had Allah willed, they would not have associated⁠﴾ [al-An'am 107], their purpose is what? The consolation of the Messenger ﷺ, because when he knows that this is by the will of Allah, he is content. But Allah the Most High refuted this claim of theirs with His words: ﴿Those who associated will say: Had Allah willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything⁠﴾. What did He say after it? ﴿Thus did those before them deny, until they tasted Our might⁠﴾ [al-An'am 148], that is, by the punishment of Allah. Allah refuted this argument, for they intended by it: what? They intended by it the nullification of the Law through the decree. So Allah the Most High made clear that He punished them. Adam was argued against by Musa, who said to him: "You have disappointed us and cast us, and yourself, out of Paradise." By what? By his disobedience, eating from the tree. Adam said to him: "Do you blame me for something that Allah wrote against me forty years before He created me?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "So Adam won the argument against him" [[Narrated by Ahmad (7635) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. In another narration: "So Adam overcame Musa in argument" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3409) and Muslim (2652) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. The meaning of "hajjahu" is that he overcame him in argument. So Adam argued by the decree that had been written for him before he was created, and Musa was refuted. Who argues with this hadith? The people of sin, for their sins, saying: Adam argued by the decree against Musa, and the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, ruled in favour of whom? In favour of Adam, and said: "He overcame him," so we argue by the decree just as our father argued. I answer this with two answers. The first answer is that of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him. He said: Adam did not argue by the decree for the sin; rather he argued by the decree for the expulsion from Paradise. As for the sin, Adam repented of it, and they said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers" [al-A'raf 23], and ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words⁠﴾ [al-Baqarah 37]. Do you understand? So Adam cannot possibly argue by the decree for the sin at all, and he is too exalted in rank to argue by the decree against the disobedience of Allah. He argued by the decree only for his expulsion from Paradise, not for the cause of the expulsion. And arguing by the decree regarding calamities is permissible, and it is the utmost submission to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Have you noticed the words of the Messenger ﷺ: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in both. Be eager for what benefits you, seek help from Allah and do not be incapable. If something befalls you, do not say: 'If only I had done such-and-such.' Rather say: 'It is the decree of Allah, and He does what He wills.'"[[Narrated by Muslim (2664 / 34) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] This is an argument by the decree, but after the action has been taken, with its causes. So arguing by the decree regarding calamities is permissible, and when a person is afflicted by a calamity and says: "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return," this means submission to the decree. Be mindful, O people, pay attention. So the argument of Adam by the decree was regarding what? Regarding the calamity, not the sin. This is one aspect. The second aspect: it was not befitting for Musa, peace be upon him, to blame his father for a sin he had repented of, after which his Lord chose him and guided him. This is not possible; even the lowest of people, if someone is afflicted by a sin and then repents, will not direct blame at him. Allah the Most High said: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. Then his Lord chose him, and accepted his repentance and guided him⁠﴾ [Ta-Ha 121-122]. This rank was not attained before the sin occurred. So it is not possible for Musa to blame his father for a sin that he repented of and that raised him in rank with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is not possible from even the lowest person, let alone a man of the resolute messengers. This is the answer of whom? The answer of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, and it is undoubtedly a good answer. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, went to another answer and said: Arguing by the decree for a sin after repenting from it and giving it up is accepted, not for the removal of blame or for permission to persist. So he says arguing by the decree is of two types. One type: arguing by the decree after the matter has passed, together with giving up the sin and good condition; this is permissible. And arguing by the decree to ward off blame and to persist in sin; this is what? It is forbidden. Do you understand? That is, if we suppose that Adam's argument by the decree for the sin from which he repented, and which Allah guided him and chose him, is permissible on this supposition, because Adam did not argue this in order to persist; he argued it because it had passed. And an example of this now, among us: if a person commits fornication, may Allah protect us, and he is a good man but his desire overcame him, then he repents, and we say to him: "O so-and-so, how did this happen to you?" He says: "By Allah, brother, it is the decree and destiny; otherwise I am not of the people of this matter, but what is decreed has occurred." Do we accept from him or not? We accept from him. But if he continued to commit fornication and we said: "Repent to Allah," he says: "By Allah, this is compulsion." Compulsion! Subhan Allah, compulsion, while you are practising this deed? That is not compulsion. In any case, Ibn al-Qayyim says: arguing by the decree after it has occurred, as submission to the decree and entrusting the matter to Allah, not to persist and not to ward off blame, is permissible. Then he cited an account that occurred with 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and his wife Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her, when the Prophet ﷺ entered upon them and said to them: "Will you not pray?" 'Ali said: "O Messenger of Allah, our souls are in the hand of Allah; if He willed, He would have raised us up." He argued by what? By the decree. So the Prophet ﷺ went out, or turned away from them, striking his thigh and saying: "And man is more than anything given to disputation."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1127) and Muslim (775 / 206).]] So did the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, accept from them or not?
Student: No, he accepted.
Shaykh: Be careful: if you say he accepted absolutely, that is not correct. If you say: he accepted the reality, but he disliked the disputation, then this is the reality, because had he wished to reject it outright, he would have said otherwise; he would have said: "There is no argument for you in this." But he treated it as part of the disputation which he had forbidden. One day he came out to his companions while they were disputing about the decree, and he became angry, as if pomegranate seeds were being squeezed in his face; his face turned red, and he forbade disputing about the decree.[[Narrated by Ibn Majah (85) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As.]] So the second way out of the story of Adam with Musa is what? That Adam argued by the decree regarding a matter that had passed and ended, and he was freed from it. But this is what I say: the first aspect is, in my opinion, stronger, because Musa cannot blame his father for a matter he repented of. But the second has a point of view, without doubt. However, we do not apply the story of Adam and Musa to it; rather we say: it applies to all people now.
